title: The Fruit of the Tree
creator: Edith Wharton
description: A nurse, a mill-town, and a mercy killing — Wharton's novel of industrial reform and moral tragedy.

title: The Reef
creator: Edith Wharton
description: An American widow in France entangled in a younger man's affair — Wharton's most psychologically intricate novel.

title: The Custom of the Country
creator: Edith Wharton
description: Undine Spragg's ruthless ascent through husbands and millions — Wharton's savage anatomy of the marriage market.

title: Summer
creator: Edith Wharton
description: Charity Royall's summer of love in the Berkshires — Wharton's boldest novel of female desire.

title: False Dawn (The 'Forties)
creator: Edith Wharton
description: 'The 'Forties' — the first Old New York novella; a young man's daring purchase of avant-garde art.

title: New Year's Day (The 'Seventies)
creator: Edith Wharton
description: 'The 'Seventies' — the final Old New York novella; a widow's secret revealed after decades.

title: The Old Maid (The 'Fifties)
creator: Edith Wharton
description: 'The 'Fifties' — Delia Ralston and her cousin's secret child; the best-known of the Old New York novellas.

title: The Spark (The 'Sixties)
creator: Edith Wharton
description: 'The 'Sixties' — a wife's belated discovery of her husband's wartime heroism.

title: A Few Figs from Thistles
creator: Edna St. Vincent Millay
description: The slim volume that made Millay famous — the flaming youth of the Jazz Age in verse.

title: Second April
creator: Edna St. Vincent Millay
description: The sonnets and lyrics of Millay's Greenwich Village maturity.

title: The Harp-Weaver and Other Poems
creator: Edna St. Vincent Millay
description: The Pulitzer volume — 'The Harp-Weaver' ballad and the sonnet sequence of Millay's prime.

title: The Children of the Night
creator: Edwin Arlington Robinson
description: 'Richard Cory,' 'Miniver Cheevy,' 'Luke Havergal' — the book that made Robinson's name.

title: The Town Down the River
creator: Edwin Arlington Robinson
description: Further Tilbury Town portraits — the essential middle Robinson collection.

title: Merlin
creator: Edwin Arlington Robinson
description: The Arthurian epic in blank verse — Robinson's most ambitious single poem.

title: Virginia
creator: Ellen Glasgow
description: Virginia Pendleton's life sacrificed to Southern womanhood — the opening of Glasgow's great sequence.

title: Barren Ground
creator: Ellen Glasgow
description: A woman's thirty-year conquest of worn-out Virginia farmland — the novel Glasgow considered her best.

title: The Romantic Comedians
creator: Ellen Glasgow
description: A judge's late marriage and its collapse — Glasgow's sharpest comedy of Southern manners.

title: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Three Series, Complete
creator: Emily Dickinson
description: All three 1890s Todd/Higginson selections in one volume — the complete public-domain record of Emily Dickinson's poetry.

title: The Single Hound
creator: Emily Dickinson
description: Martha Bianchi's selection from the family manuscripts — the first new Dickinson book of the modernist era.

title: Three Stories and Ten Poems
creator: Ernest Hemingway
description: The 1923 Paris debut — 'Up in Michigan' and the first Nick Adams stories; where Hemingway began.

title: In Our Time
creator: Ernest Hemingway
description: The stories that changed American prose — Nick Adams from Michigan to the war; the founding book of the Hemingway style.

title: The Torrents of Spring
creator: Ernest Hemingway
description: The Anderson parody that ended a mentorship — Hemingway's comic novella and publishing gambit.

title: Men Without Women
creator: Ernest Hemingway
description: Fourteen stories including 'The Killers' and 'Hills Like White Elephants' — the essential Hemingway book.

title: Exultations
creator: Ezra Pound
description: Troubadour songs and early lyrics — the medievalist Pound emerging beside the modernist.

title: Personae
creator: Ezra Pound
description: The 1909 London collection — the young American's bid for poetic mastery, the root of Imagism.

title: Canzoni & Ripostes
creator: Ezra Pound
description: The combined 1913 volume — Canzoni with the Ripostes appendix of Hulme's poems; the book that launched Imagism.

title: Lustra
creator: Ezra Pound
description: The 1916 collection of satires and epigrams — Pound's London modernism at its sharpest.

title: Hugh Selwyn Mauberley
creator: Ezra Pound
description: The eighteen-poem sequence bidding farewell to a civilization — Pound's masterpiece of the postwar reckoning.

title: Flappers and Philosophers
creator: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Eight stories including 'Bernice Bobs Her Hair' — the flapper canon in its first collected form.

title: This Side of Paradise
creator: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Amory Blaine's Princeton-to-war youth — the book that named a generation and invented the Jazz Age novel.

title: The Beautiful and Damned
creator: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: The beautiful young couple rotting on expectation — Fitzgerald's darkest Jazz Age novel.

title: Tales of the Jazz Age
creator: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Eleven stories including 'May Day' and 'The Diamond as Big as the Ritz' — the Jazz Age at full volume.

title: McTeague
creator: Frank Norris
description: The dentist's descent into murderous avarice in Polk Street — the masterpiece of American naturalism.

title: The Octopus
creator: Frank Norris
description: The Southern Pacific Railroad as the tentacled monopoly crushing the wheat ranchers — the founding novel of the American protest epic.

title: The Pit
creator: Frank Norris
description: The Chicago wheat pit and a speculator's corner — the great American novel of finance, completing the wheat trilogy's arc.

title: Daisy Miller
creator: Henry James
description: The American girl in Rome — the story that made Henry James's name and defined the American-abroad theme for a century.

title: Washington Square
creator: Henry James
description: The plain heiress, the fortune-hunter, and the tyrannical father — James's flawless novella-length tragedy of filial obedience.

title: The Portrait of a Lady — Volume 1
creator: Henry James
description: Volume 1 of James's first masterpiece — Isabel Archer's inheritance and European education.

title: The Portrait of a Lady — Volume 2
creator: Henry James
description: Volume 2 of James's first masterpiece — the fatal marriage to Osmond and its reckoning.

title: The Bostonians — Volume 1
creator: Henry James
description: Volume 1 — the battle for the feminist orator Verena Tarrant begins.

title: The Bostonians — Volume 2
creator: Henry James
description: Volume 2 — reform, love, and Verena's choice.

title: The Turn of the Screw
creator: Henry James
description: The governess, the children, the ghosts at Bly — the most argued-about novella in English, horror's great ambiguous masterpiece.

title: The Wings of the Dove — Volume 1
creator: Henry James
description: Volume 1 of the first late masterpiece — Kate, Densher, and the dying heiress Milly Theale.

title: The Wings of the Dove — Volume 2
creator: Henry James
description: Volume 2 — Venice, the deception, and Milly's posthumous victory.

title: The Ambassadors
creator: Henry James
description: Strether's belated European education in Paris — the novel James himself ranked first among his works.

title: The Golden Bowl
creator: Henry James
description: Maggie Verver's discovery of her husband's affair — the densest, most architectonic novel James ever wrote.

title: Evangeline
creator: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
description: The tale of the Acadian lovers parted by the British expulsion — the American epic in English hexameters, memorized by generations.

title: The Song of Hiawatha
creator: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
description: Longfellow's trochaic epic of Hiawatha — the single most-read American poem of the 19th century, for better and worse the national myth of the 'noble savage.'

title: The Courtship of Miles Standish
creator: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
description: The Pilgrim love-triangle of Miles Standish, John Alden, and Priscilla — the verse epic that made Plymouth the American origin story.

title: Tales of a Wayside Inn
creator: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
description: The frame-tale collection whose 'Paul Revere's Ride' became the most recited poem in America — Longfellow's Canterbury Tales.

title: The Son of the Wolf
creator: Jack London
description: The debut story collection — the first Klondike tales, the book that made Jack London's name.

title: The People of the Abyss
creator: Jack London
description: Seven weeks disguised as a sailor in the East End slums — the book that invented immersive social reportage.

title: Love of Life and Other Stories
creator: Jack London
description: The starving prospector crawling to survival — with 'The Story of Keesh' and other essential later stories.

title: The Road
creator: Jack London
description: Riding the rails as a teenage tramp — the memoir that made the hobo an American literary figure.

title: South Sea Tales
creator: Jack London
description: Tales of the Solomon Islands and the leper colony — London's Pacific fiction at its most brutal and humane.

title: John Barleycorn
creator: Jack London
description: London's confessional of a lifetime's drinking — the first major American memoir of alcoholism.

title: The Spy
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: A Revolutionary War tale of espionage and divided loyalties; the novel that proved American fiction could outsell British imports on American soil.

title: The Pioneers
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: The first Leatherstocking tale — old Natty Bumppo confronts the settlement of the wilderness he helped open; the founding novel of the American frontier myth.

title: The Pilot
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: A Revolutionary War sea-adventure modeled on John Paul Jones; the first sea novel in American literature and the direct ancestor of Moby-Dick's tradition.

title: The Last of the Mohicans
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: Hawkeye, Chingachgook, and Uncas in the French and Indian War — the archetypal American adventure novel, still the most-translated early American book.

title: The Prairie
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: The aged Natty Bumppo dies facing west on the prairie — the elegiac close of Cooper's frontier epic and the first great American novel of the West.

title: The Pathfinder
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: Natty Bumppo as scout on Lake Ontario in the Seven Years' War — the essential middle volume of the Leatherstocking Tales.

title: The Deerslayer
creator: James Fenimore Cooper
description: Young Natty Bumppo's first war-path on Glimmerglass — the genesis volume of the Leatherstocking Tales and the template of the American hero's moral code.

title: The Biglow Papers
creator: James Russell Lowell
description: Hosea Biglow's Yankee-dialect satires on the Mexican War — the masterpiece of American comic verse and the ancestor of all dialect poetry.

title: A Fable for Critics
creator: James Russell Lowell
description: Lowell's galloping survey of his contemporaries — Poe, Emerson, Hawthorne judged in verse; the founding document of American critical reputation-making.

title: The Vision of Sir Launfal
creator: James Russell Lowell
description: The Grail quest as moral allegory, containing 'The Present Crisis' — the poem that gave abolitionism its battle-cry.

title: In War Time, and Other Poems
creator: John Greenleaf Whittier
description: Whittier's Civil War collection, including 'Barbara Frietchie' — the abolitionist bard's wartime voice at full power.

title: Snow-Bound
creator: John Greenleaf Whittier
description: A family snowed in around the hearth — the great American fireside poem and Whittier's most perfect work.

title: Bayou Folk
creator: Kate Chopin
description: Twenty-three Louisiana stories including 'Désirée's Baby' — the founding collection of Creole local color.

title: A Night in Acadie
creator: Kate Chopin
description: Further Acadian tales — the essential companion to Bayou Folk.

title: The Awakening
creator: Kate Chopin
description: Edna Pontellier's awakening in Creole Louisiana — the novel that invented modern feminist fiction.

title: Not Without Laughter
creator: Langston Hughes
description: Sandy Rogers's coming of age — the classic novel of the Harlem Renaissance's Midwestern roots.

title: The Autocrat of the Breakfast-Table
creator: Oliver Wendell Holmes
description: The breakfast-table monologues that made Holmes famous — the founding text of American familiar-essay wit.

title: The Professor at the Breakfast-Table
creator: Oliver Wendell Holmes
description: The Autocrat's successor volume, containing 'The Chambered Nautilus' — Holmes's meditation on the soul's expansion.

title: Elsie Venner
creator: Oliver Wendell Holmes
description: A girl tainted by prenatal snakebite — Holmes's novel of heredity and moral responsibility, the first American novel of biological determinism.

title: Mountain Interval
creator: Robert Frost
description: 'The Road Not Taken,' 'Birches,' 'The Oven Bird' — the book that made Frost America's poet.

title: New Hampshire
creator: Robert Frost
description: The Pulitzer volume containing 'Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening' and 'Fire and Ice.'

title: Poor White
creator: Sherwood Anderson
description: Hugh McVey's machines remake Bidwell, Ohio — Anderson's novel of the industrial revolution's human price.

title: Many Marriages
creator: Sherwood Anderson
description: A manufacturer's midnight confession of erotic discontent — the most outspoken of Anderson's novels.

title: Dark Laughter
creator: Sherwood Anderson
description: The journalist who flees civilization for the 'dark laughter' of instinct — the novel Hemingway parodied.

title: The Science of English Verse
creator: Sidney Lanier
description: Lanier's lectures treating poetry as scored music — the first systematic American prosody, by the South's poet-flautist.

title: The Poems of Sidney Lanier
creator: Sidney Lanier
description: The posthumous collection containing 'The Marshes of Glynn' and 'The Symphony' — the South's great musical poet at full stretch.

title: Arrowsmith
creator: Sinclair Lewis
description: Martin Arrowsmith's war between research and commerce — the novel that made the scientist a tragic American hero.

title: Elmer Gantry
creator: Sinclair Lewis
description: The evangelist as magnificent fraud — the satire that made religious hucksterism an American archetype.

title: The Man Who Knew Coolidge
creator: Sinclair Lewis
description: Lowell Schmaltz's endless monologue on knowing Coolidge — the comic pendant to Babbitt.

title: Dodsworth
creator: Sinclair Lewis
description: Sam Dodsworth's retirement and his wife's restlessness in Europe — the mature masterpiece of Lewis's middle period.

title: Maggie: A Girl of the Streets
creator: Stephen Crane
description: The first unflinching American slum novel — the founding text of literary naturalism in the United States.

title: The Red Badge of Courage
creator: Stephen Crane
description: Henry Fleming's terror and flight at Chancellorsville — the novel that invented modern war fiction.

title: The Open Boat and Other Stories
creator: Stephen Crane
description: The shipwreck-survival masterpiece 'The Open Boat' with 'The Bride Comes to Yellow Sky' — Crane's essential short fiction.

title: Jennie Gerhardt
creator: Theodore Dreiser
description: The laundress who sacrifices everything for love — Dreiser's most tender and morally complex novel.

title: The Financier
creator: Theodore Dreiser
description: Frank Cowperwood's ruthless rise in Philadelphia — the first volume of Dreiser's trilogy of American capitalism.

title: The Titan
creator: Theodore Dreiser
description: Cowperwood's Chicago streetcar empire — the middle volume of the Trilogy of Desire.

title: The 'Genius'
creator: Theodore Dreiser
description: The artist Eugene Witla's erotic and artistic education — the novel suppressed as obscene, Dreiser's most autobiographical work.

title: Look Homeward, Angel
creator: Thomas Wolfe
description: Eugene Gant's vast hunger for life in Altamont — the most exuberant debut in American fiction.

title: The Jungle
creator: Upton Sinclair
description: Jurgis Rudkus in the Chicago stockyards — the exposé that forced the Pure Food and Drug Act through Congress.

title: King Coal
creator: Upton Sinclair
description: The undercover organizer in the Colorado coalfields — Sinclair's novel of the mine wars.

title: The Brass Check
creator: Upton Sinclair
description: Sinclair's exposé of American newspaper corruption — the first systematic American critique of the press.

title: Oil!
creator: Upton Sinclair
description: The Teapot Dome-era epic of oil, labor, and Hollywood — the novel behind 'There Will Be Blood.'

title: Knickerbocker's History of New York — Volume 1
creator: Washington Irving
description: Volume 1 of the mock-chronicle of Dutch New Amsterdam.

title: Knickerbocker's History of New York — Volume 2
creator: Washington Irving
description: Volume 2 of the mock-chronicle of Dutch New Amsterdam.

title: The Sketch Book of Geoffrey Crayon
creator: Washington Irving
description: The collection that made American literature a fact on the world stage — Rip Van Winkle, the Legend of Sleepy Hollow, and the Christmas sketches that invented the modern American holiday mythos.

title: Tales of the Alhambra
creator: Washington Irving
description: Sketches and legends gathered in Granada's Alhambra — the founding American travel book about Europe, and the source of Spain's romantic myth in English.

title: The Song of the Lark
creator: Willa Cather
description: Thea Kronborg's ascent from a Colorado railroad town to prima donna — the definitive American novel of the artist's formation.

title: One of Ours
creator: Willa Cather
description: Claude Wheeler's escape from Nebraska into the Great War — the Pulitzer-winning novel of America's war awakening.

title: A Lost Lady
creator: Willa Cather
description: The fading belle of the Nebraska frontier — Cather's most perfectly proportioned elegy.

title: The Professor's House
creator: Willa Cather
description: Godfrey St. Peter's midlife reckoning, enclosing the mesa-country masterpiece 'Tom Outland's Story.'

title: Death Comes for the Archbishop
creator: Willa Cather
description: Two French priests in 19th-century New Mexico — the luminous epic of faith and landscape.

title: Al Que Quiere!
creator: William Carlos Williams
description: The 1917 collection that announced Williams's American idiom — the foundation of his life's work.

title: Sour Grapes
creator: William Carlos Williams
description: The essential middle book — the Rutherford doctor-poet finding his full voice.

title: Poems (Bryant, 1821)
creator: William Cullen Bryant
description: The slim volume containing 'Thanatopsis,' written at seventeen — the first American poetry to be taken seriously abroad, and the seed of American nature poetry.

title: The Rise of Silas Lapham
creator: William Dean Howells
description: The paint-millionaire's moral rise and fall in Boston — the novel that established realism as America's serious fictional mode.

title: A Hazard of New Fortunes
creator: William Dean Howells
description: Basil March's move to New York and a socialist's martyrdom — the founding novel of urban American realism.

title: Soldiers' Pay
creator: William Faulkner
description: The first Faulkner novel — a dying flier comes home to Georgia; the beginning of the Yoknapatawpha journey.

title: Mosquitoes
creator: William Faulkner
description: A yacht party of New Orleans artists — Faulkner's satiric second novel, the bridge to his maturity.

title: Sartoris
creator: William Faulkner
description: The decayed Sartoris family of Jefferson — the first novel of Yoknapatawpha County.

title: As I Lay Dying
creator: William Faulkner
description: Fifteen narrators carry Addie Bundren to Jefferson — the polyphonic masterpiece of high American modernism.

title: The Eatonville Anthology
creator: Zora Neale Hurston
description: Fourteen Eatonville character sketches from the Messenger (1926) — the firstfruits of Hurston's anthropological fiction.

title: Sweat
creator: Zora Neale Hurston
source: Project Gutenberg ebook #71448 (Fire!! magazine, story extracted)
description: Delia Jones, the washerwoman, and her snake of a husband — the defining short story of the Harlem Renaissance, from Fire!! (1926).

title: Cudjo's Own Story of the Last African Slaver
creator: Zora Neale Hurston
description: Hurston's 1927 Journal of Negro History interview with Cudjo Lewis, last survivor of the Clotilda — the raw primary source of Barracoon.

title: How It Feels to Be Colored Me
creator: Zora Neale Hurston
description: Hurston's 1928 World Tomorrow essay — the triumphant declaration of Black identity that became the Harlem Renaissance's most quoted personal statement.

title: Phèdre
creator: Jean Racine
description: Racine's supreme tragedy — Phèdre's fatal passion for Hippolyte, the summit of French neoclassical theater. French original (Didot 1854 edition) — no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Aurélia
creator: Gérard de Nerval
description: Nerval's dream-autobiography of madness and vision — the surrealists' bible, companion to batch 07's Sylvie. French original — no public-domain English translation exists (Aldington 1932 still in copyright).

title: Illuminations
creator: Arthur Rimbaud
description: Rimbaud's prose-poem 'coloured plates' — the charter of modern poetry, companion to batch 07's Season in Hell. French original, 1886 La Vogue edition — no public-domain English translation exists.

title: Poésies
creator: Stéphane Mallarmé
description: Mallarmé's collected poems — the high Symbolist summit: 'L'Après-midi d'un faune,' 'Le Cygne,' the sonnets. French original, 1887 edition — no public-domain English translation exists.

title: The Cid
creator: Pierre Corneille
description: Corneille's thunderously successful tragicomedy of honor and love — the play that provoked the Querelle du Cid and defined French classical drama. Translated by Roscoe Mongan (1896).

title: The Dramatic Works of Molière, Vol. I
creator: Molière
description: Vol. I of van Laun's complete English Molière: The Blunderer, The Love-Tiff, The Pretentious Young Ladies, Sganarelle, Don Garcia of Navarre. Translated by Henri van Laun (1875).

title: The Dramatic Works of Molière, Vol. II
creator: Molière
description: Vol. II of van Laun's complete English Molière: The School for Husbands, The Bores, The School for Wives (+ Criticised), The Impromptu of Versailles, The Forced Marriage. Translated by Henri van Laun (1875).

title: The Dramatic Works of Molière, Vol. III
creator: Molière
description: Vol. III of van Laun's complete English Molière: The Princess of Elis, Don Juan, Love is the Best Doctor, The Misanthrope, The Physician in Spite of Himself. Translated by Henri van Laun (1875).

title: The Dramatic Works of Molière, Vol. IV
creator: Molière
description: Vol. IV of van Laun's complete English Molière: Mélicerte, The Sicilian, Tartuffe, Amphitryon, George Dandin. Translated by Henri van Laun (1876).

title: The Dramatic Works of Molière, Vol. V
creator: Molière
description: Vol. V of van Laun's complete English Molière: The Miser, Monsieur de Pourceaugnac, The Magnificent Lovers, The Citizen Who Apes the Nobleman, Psyche. Translated by Henri van Laun (1876).

title: The Dramatic Works of Molière, Vol. VI
creator: Molière
description: Vol. VI of van Laun's complete English Molière: The Rogueries of Scapin, The Countess of Escarbagnas, The Learned Ladies, The Imaginary Invalid, and the early farces. Translated by Henri van Laun (1876).

title: Fables of La Fontaine
creator: Jean de La Fontaine
description: The complete Fables in Wright's classic verse translation — the foundation-stone of French fabulist literature, all twelve books. Translated by Elizur Wright (1841).

title: Pensées
creator: Blaise Pascal
description: Pascal's posthumous fragments — the wager, the thinking reed, the heart's reasons: the most quoted devotional-philosophical work in French. Translated by W. F. Trotter (1910).

title: The Provincial Letters
creator: Blaise Pascal
description: Pascal's eighteen (plus two fragmentary) letters demolishing Jesuit casuistry — the prose masterpiece that made French satire an art form. Translated by George Pearce (1849).

title: Maxims and Reflections
creator: François de La Rochefoucauld
description: All 504 maxims — the cold-eyed anatomy of amour-propre that invented the French moralist tradition. Translated by John Heard, Jr. (1917).

title: The Confessions of Jean-Jacques Rousseau
creator: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
description: The complete Confessions in twelve books — the founding text of modern autobiography and Romantic self-exposure. Anonymous English translation (1903 Aldus Society edition).

title: Dangerous Acquaintances (Les Liaisons dangereuses)
creator: Choderlos de Laclos
description: The great French epistolary novel of seduction and ruin — Valmont and Merteuil's cold war, in Aldington's 1924 translation. Translated by Richard Aldington (1924).

title: One of Cleopatra's Nights and Other Fantastic Romances
creator: Théophile Gautier
description: Six tales of the fantastic — Clarimonde the vampire, Arria Marcella, The Mummy's Foot — in Hearn's lush 1882 translation; the founding texts of French fantastique. Translated by Lafcadio Hearn (1882).

title: Jean-Christophe, Vol. I: Dawn, Morning, Youth, Revolt
creator: Romain Rolland
description: Vol. I (books 1–4) of the Nobel-winning roman-fleuve: the making of the musician Jean-Christophe Krafft. Translated by Gilbert Cannan (1910).

title: Jean-Christophe in Paris: The Market-Place, Antoinette, the House
creator: Romain Rolland
description: Vol. II (books 5–7): Christophe's Paris years — the market-place of letters, Antoinette, the house on the hill. Translated by Gilbert Cannan (1911).

title: Jean-Christophe: Journey's End
creator: Romain Rolland
description: Vol. III (books 8–10): Love and Friendship, The Burning Bush, The New Dawn — the close of the ten-book cycle. Translated by Gilbert Cannan (1913).

title: Within a Budding Grove
creator: Marcel Proust
description: Vol. 2 of In Search of Lost Time: Balbec, the young girls in flower, and the first disillusionments — completing batch 07's Swann's Way in Moncrieff's translation. Translated by C. K. Scott Moncrieff (1924).

title: The Guermantes Way
creator: Marcel Proust
description: Vol. 3 of In Search of Lost Time: the Faubourg Saint-Germain, salon warfare, and the Dreyfus Affair as social X-ray. Translated by C. K. Scott Moncrieff (1925).

title: Cities of the Plain
creator: Marcel Proust
description: Vol. 4 of In Search of Lost Time (both parts): Charlus unmasked and Sodom revealed — the novel's darkest comedy. Translated by C. K. Scott Moncrieff (1927).

title: The Captive
creator: Marcel Proust
description: Vol. 5 of In Search of Lost Time: Albertine imprisoned in Paris — jealousy anatomized across a thousand pages of suspicion. Translated by C. K. Scott Moncrieff (1929).

title: The Sweet Cheat Gone
creator: Marcel Proust
description: Vol. 6 of In Search of Lost Time: Albertine gone — mourning, forgetting, and the long road toward Time Regained. Translated by C. K. Scott Moncrieff (1930).

title: The Immoralist
creator: André Gide
description: Gide's récit of Michel's liberation into amorality — the book that made him the conscience (and scandal) of French letters. Translated by Dorothy Bussy (1930).

title: The Counterfeiters
creator: André Gide
description: Gide's only 'novel' proper — the mise-en-abyme of counterfeit coin, counterfeit selves, and the novelist writing the novel. Translated by Dorothy Bussy (1927).

title: Strait is the Gate
creator: André Gide
description: Alissa and Jérôme's renunciant love — Gide's most perfect récit, in the first English translation. Translated by Dorothy Bussy (1924).

title: The Duel
creator: Alexander Kuprin
description: The novel that exposed the Tsarist officer corps — Kuprin's protest made him the most-read Russian novelist of 1905. [Translation: English translation (first published 1916).]

title: Yama (The Pit)
creator: Alexander Kuprin
description: The brothel novel — 'the first and last honest book on prostitution'; banned, devoured, and world-famous. [Translation: Bernard Guilbert Guerney (1922).]

title: The Lady with the Dog and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: The title story is the most famous love story in Russian literature. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1917).]

title: The Party and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Party,' 'A Doctor's Visit' — the great middle-period stories. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1917).]

title: The Wife, and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Wife,' 'Difficult People,' 'The Grasshopper.' [Translation: Constance Garnett (1918).]

title: The Witch, and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Witch,' 'Peasants,' 'In the Ravine' — Chekhov's peasant world at its darkest. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1918).]

title: The Bishop and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Bishop,' 'The Letter,' 'Easter Eve.' [Translation: Constance Garnett (1919).]

title: The Chorus Girl and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Chorus Girl,' 'Verotchka' — the early masterpieces. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1920).]

title: The Cook's Wedding and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Cook's Wedding,' 'The Dependents,' 'The Orator.' [Translation: Constance Garnett (1921).]

title: The Horse-Stealers and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Horse-Stealers,' 'The Privy Councillor' — the steppe stories. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1921).]

title: The Schoolmaster and Other Stories
creator: Anton Chekhov
description: 'The Schoolmaster,' 'The Horse-Stealers,' 'The Man in a Case.' [Translation: Constance Garnett (1921).]

title: The Devil's Elixir, Vol. 1
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: Hoffmann's doppelgänger monk novel, vol. 1 — the founding text of the double in modern literature, translated the decade it appeared. [Translation: R. P. Gillies (1824).]

title: The Devil's Elixir, Vol. 2
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: Conclusion of Hoffmann's doppelgänger novel — both volumes staged per the completeness gate. [Translation: R. P. Gillies (1824).]

title: The Serapion Brethren, Vol. I
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: Hoffmann's great story-cycle, vol. I — the frame-tale model for the 19th-century fantastic, in Ewing's classic translation. [Translation: Alexander Ewing (1886).]

title: The Serapion Brethren, Vol. II
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: The story-cycle concluded — both Ewing volumes staged per the completeness gate. [Translation: Alexander Ewing (1892).]

title: Lebensansichten des Katers Murr (The Life and Opinions of the Tomcat Murr)
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: Hoffmann's last, greatest novel — the tomcat's autobiography interleaved with Kapellmeister Kreisler's; the first modernist collage-novel. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: Weird Tales, Vol. 1
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: Bealby's selection of Hoffmann's uncanny tales, vol. 1 — the stories that taught Poe and Gogol the fantastic. [Translation: J. T. Bealby (1885).]

title: Weird Tales, Vol. 2
creator: E. T. A. Hoffmann
description: Bealby's selection, vol. 2 — both volumes staged per the completeness gate. [Translation: J. T. Bealby (1885).]

title: Das Schloß (The Castle)
creator: Franz Kafka
description: K.'s struggle with the Castle — the great unfinished novel of bureaucratic night, from the 1926 first edition. No PD English translation exists; staged in German. [Translation: German original, first edition (Kurt Wolff, 1926; no PD English translation).]

title: Hyperion; or, The Hermit in Greece
creator: Friedrich Hölderlin
description: Hölderlin's only novel — the epistolary hymn to Greece that German Romanticism is built on. No PD English translation exists (Trask 1965, Benjamin 2008); staged in the German original from the 1822 second edition. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation exists; earliest English trans. 1965).]

title: The Robbers
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The Sturm und Drang explosion — Karl Moor's robber band made the 21-year-old Schiller famous overnight and invented European melodrama. [Translation: Alexander Fraser Tytler (1792).]

title: Fiesco; or, the Genoese Conspiracy
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's republican tragedy of conspiracy in Genoa — the young playwright's study of political ambition and betrayal. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: Love and Intrigue
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Kabale und Liebe — the bourgeois tragedy that made class oppression stageable; the most performed of Schiller's early plays. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: Don Carlos
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The Spanish Inquisition tragedy behind Verdi's opera — Schiller's great drama of freedom of thought versus power. [Translation: R. D. Boylan (19th c.).]

title: History of the Revolt of the Netherlands
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's history of the Dutch revolt against Spain — the companion history to the Thirty Years' War, and the background of Don Carlos. [Translation: Edward Backhouse Eastwick (19th c.).]

title: The Ghost-Seer; or, the Apparitionist
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's unfinished gothic novel of secret societies and apparitions — a founding text of the German Schauerroman and the conspiracy thriller. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: History of the Thirty Years' War
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The history that won Schiller his Jena professorship — the standard 19th-century account of Europe's great religious war, and the research behind Wallenstein. [Translation: A. J. W. Morrison (1846).]

title: Wallensteins Lager
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The prologue of the Wallenstein trilogy, in the original German — the soldiers' camp before the fall. Staged in German to complete the trilogy; no PD English standalone exists. [Translation: German original (no PD English standalone; Churchill's translation exists only in Bohn's complete Works).]

title: The Death of Wallenstein
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The climax of the trilogy in Coleridge's translation — Wallenstein's fall is the summit of German classical drama. [Translation: Samuel Taylor Coleridge (1800).]

title: The Piccolomini
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Part two of the Wallenstein trilogy, translated by Coleridge himself — the great English Romantic rendering of Schiller's Thirty Years' War epic. [Translation: Samuel Taylor Coleridge (1800).]

title: Mary Stuart
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The queens' tragedy — Mary and Elizabeth's confrontation is the classic drama of female power and fate. [Translation: Joseph Mellish (1801).]

title: The Maid of Orleans
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's Joan of Arc — the romantic tragedy that fixed Joan's image for the 19th century; source for Verdi's and Tchaikovsky's operas. [Translation: Anna Swanwick (19th c.).]

title: The Bride of Messina
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's attempt to revive the Greek chorus on the modern stage, with his famous essay 'On the Use of the Chorus in Tragedy' appended. [Translation: A. Lodge (19th c.).]

title: William Tell
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's last completed play — the Swiss liberation drama that made Tell a world symbol of resistance to tyranny. [Translation: Theodore Martin (19th c.).]

title: The Poems of Schiller: First Period
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: Schiller's early lyrics, including the poems embedded in The Robbers — the Sturm und Drang voice before Weimar classicism. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: The Poems of Schiller: Second Period
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The middle-period poems — 'The Song of the Bell' era; Schiller at the height of his lyric power. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: The Poems of Schiller: Suppressed Poems
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The poems Schiller suppressed — the unguarded early voice, completing the four-volume Bohn poetry set. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: The Poems of Schiller: Third Period
creator: Friedrich Schiller
description: The late philosophical ballads — 'The Diver,' 'The Glove,' the great Weimar poems on freedom and fate. [Translation: Bohn's Standard Library translation (1846-47).]

title: Dantons Tod (Danton's Death)
creator: Georg Büchner
description: The French Revolution tragedy written at 21 — the birth of modern political drama. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: Leonce und Lena; Lenz
creator: Georg Büchner
description: Büchner's comedy of bored princes and his shattering Lenz novella — the two shorter masterpieces, in the German Insel edition. [Translation: German original (Insel-Bücherei, 1925).]

title: Der grüne Heinrich (Green Henry)
creator: Gottfried Keller
description: Keller's autobiographical artist-novel — the great Swiss Bildungsroman, beside Wilhelm Meister and Nachsommer. No PD English translation; staged in German from Projekt Gutenberg-DE. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation on PG; Projekt Gutenberg-DE text).]

title: Seldwyla Folks: Three Singular Tales
creator: Gottfried Keller
description: Three tales from Die Leute von Seldwyla — including 'A Village Romeo and Juliet,' the most famous German village tragedy. [Translation: Wolf von Schierbrand (1919).]

title: Laocoon: An Essay upon the Limits of Painting and Poetry
creator: Gotthold Ephraim Lessing
description: The founding text of modern aesthetics — Lessing's division of the arts of space and time, the basis of all later art theory. [Translation: Ellen Frothingham (1873).]

title: Minna von Barnhelm
creator: Gotthold Ephraim Lessing
description: The first great German comedy — the Seven Years' War veteran and his proud fiancée; the model for all German comedy after it. [Translation: Ernest Bell (1878).]

title: Nathan the Wise
creator: Gotthold Ephraim Lessing
description: Lessing's plea for religious tolerance — the Ring Parable is the Enlightenment's definitive statement against fanaticism. First English translation (1791). [Translation: William Taylor (1791).]

title: The Dramatic Works of G. E. Lessing
creator: Gotthold Ephraim Lessing
description: Miss Sara Sampson, Philotas, Emilia Galotti, Nathan the Wise — the four plays that made Lessing the founder of modern German drama. Bell's translation differs from Taylor's 1791 Nathan; both staged as significant translations. [Translation: Ernest Bell (1878).]

title: Atta Troll
creator: Heinrich Heine
description: Heine's mock-epic of the dancing bear — the great verse satire on German political poetry and its philistines. [Translation: Herman George Scheffauer (1913).]

title: The Poems of Heine: Complete
creator: Heinrich Heine
description: The complete Heine in English — the Book of Songs and all the lyrics that Schubert, Schumann, and every German schoolchild know. [Translation: Edgar Alfred Bowring (1861).]

title: The Prose Writings of Heinrich Heine
creator: Heinrich Heine
description: Ellis's selection — Reisebilder, The Romantic School, Florentine Nights, The Gods in Exile: Heine the prose ironist at full stretch. [Translation: Havelock Ellis edition (1887).]

title: Der Zerbrochene Krug (The Broken Jug)
creator: Heinrich von Kleist
description: Kleist's great comedy of the corrupt village judge — the masterpiece of German comic drama. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: Penthesilea
creator: Heinrich von Kleist
description: Kleist's savage Amazon tragedy — Achilles torn apart by the queen who loves him; the most extreme play of German Romanticism. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: Peter Camenzind
creator: Hermann Hesse
description: Hesse's first success — the village boy's failed search for the artist's life. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: The Village
creator: Ivan Bunin
description: Bunin's bleak peasant novel — the book that split the Russian intelligentsia and foreshadowed his Nobel. [Translation: Isabel Hapgood (1923).]

title: The Gentleman from San Francisco, and Other Stories
creator: Ivan Bunin
description: The title story is the great Russian short story of the 20th century — the American millionaire's death at Capri; translated with D. H. Lawrence. [Translation: D. H. Lawrence, S. S. Koteliansky & Leonard Woolf (1922, Hogarth Press).]

title: The Jew and Other Stories
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: Early stories including the Napoleonic tales — Turgenev before the great novels. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1890s-1910s).]

title: The Diary of a Superfluous Man, and Other Stories
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: The title story invents the 'superfluous man' — the archetype of Russian literature; Garnett's 1899 translation. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1899).]

title: A House of Gentlefolk
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: Lavretsky and Liza — Turgenev's most lyrical novel, the elegy for the Russian gentry. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1890s-1910s).]

title: First Love, and Other Stories
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: First Love and companion stories in Hapgood's 1904 translation — staged alongside the Garnett Turgenevs as a significant different translation. [Translation: Isabel Hapgood (1904).]

title: On the Eve
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: The Bulgarian revolutionary Insarov and Elena — Turgenev's novel of the 'new man' on the eve of emancipation. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1890s-1910s).]

title: Smoke
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: The Baden-Baden novel — Turgenev's savage satire of the Russian émigré 'smoke' and the nihilist generation. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1890s-1910s).]

title: The Torrents of Spring
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: The Frankfurt novella — a man's life ruined by one passion; Turgenev's most perfect short novel. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1890s-1910s).]

title: Virgin Soil
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: Turgenev's last novel — the populist movement of the 1870s; staged in Townsend's translation alongside the Garnett Turgenevs as a significant different translation. [Translation: R. S. Townsend (1917).]

title: Dream Tales and Prose Poems
creator: Ivan Turgenev
description: Turgenev's late mystical tales and the prose poems — the strange, visionary side of the realist. [Translation: Constance Garnett (1890s-1910s).]

title: The Red Laugh
creator: Leonid Andreyev
description: Fragments of a discovered manuscript — the Russo-Japanese War as apocalyptic hallucination; the first great anti-war expressionist text. [Translation: Alexandra Linden (1903).]

title: Savva and the Life of Man
creator: Leonid Andreyev
description: Two plays — the anarchist Savva and the allegorical Life of Man; Andreyev the dramatist at his most ambitious. [Translation: Thomas Seltzer (1920).]

title: The Seven Who Were Hanged
creator: Leonid Andreyev
description: Seven condemned terrorists await the gallows — the story that made Andreyev world-famous; Tolstoy's generation debated it for years. [Translation: Herman Bernstein (1909).]

title: King Hunger
creator: Leonid Andreyev
description: The allegorical revolt of the starving — Andreyev's most radical stage vision, from Poet Lore's Winter 1911 issue. [Translation: Eugene M. Kayden (1911, Poet Lore).]

title: He Who Gets Slapped
creator: Leonid Andreyev
description: The circus clown tragedy — Andreyev's most performed play in English; the Theatre Guild's 1922 New York hit. [Translation: Gregory Zilboorg (1922).]

title: Creatures That Once Were Men
creator: Maxim Gorky
description: Chelkash, Twenty-six Men and a Girl, and the doss-house stories — Gorky's tramps made him world-famous. [Translation: J. K. M. Shirazi (1905).]

title: The Lower Depths
creator: Maxim Gorky
description: The flophouse play — Stanislavsky's Moscow Art Theatre triumph; the great Russian drama of the dispossessed. [Translation: Jenny Covan (1922).]

title: Mother
creator: Maxim Gorky
description: The founding novel of Socialist Realism — Pelageya Vlasova's road to revolution; first published in English in 1906. [Translation: Anonymous English translation (1906-07, D. Appleton).]

title: My Childhood
creator: Maxim Gorky
description: Volume one of the autobiography — the brutal, vivid Nizhny Novgorod childhood; a landmark of Russian memoir. [Translation: English translation (1915, The Century Co.).]

title: In the World
creator: Maxim Gorky
description: Volume two of the autobiographical trilogy — the young Gorky's vagabond years among Russia's outcasts. [Translation: Gertrude M. Foakes (1917).]

title: Hymns to the Night
creator: Novalis
description: Six hymns on night, death, and the beloved — the summit of German Romantic poetry, written after Sophie von Kühn's death. Extracted complete from MacDonald's Rampolli (1897). [Translation: George MacDonald (1897).]

title: Henry of Ofterdingen: A Romance
creator: Novalis
description: The unfinished Romantic novel of the Blue Flower — the central symbol of German Romantic longing, published posthumously by Tieck. [Translation: English translation, 1842.]

title: The Disciples at Saïs and Other Fragments
creator: Novalis
description: Novalis's nature-philosophy romance-fragment and the famous fragments — the Romantic theory of poetry in its purest form. Birch's 1903 Methuen translation. [Translation: Una Birch (1903).]

title: Das Buch der Bilder (The Book of Images)
creator: Rainer Maria Rilke
description: Rilke's early lyric book — the poems before the Elegies; the fountainhead of modern German poetry. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: Die Aufzeichnungen des Malte Laurids Brigge
creator: Rainer Maria Rilke
description: Rilke's only novel — the Paris notebooks; the first modernist novel of consciousness in German. No PD English translation exists; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation; first English trans. 1930).]

title: Trials and Tribulations (Irrungen, Wirrungen)
creator: Theodor Fontane
description: On Tangled Paths — the great Berlin novel of love across the class divide, in Katharine Royce's 1917 translation for the Harvard Classics Shelf of Fiction. [Translation: Katharine Royce (1917).]

title: Frau Jenny Treibel
creator: Theodor Fontane
description: Fontane's comedy of bourgeois social climbing in Berlin — the subtlest German society novel of the 19th century. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: Immensee
creator: Theodor Storm
description: Storm's beloved first novella — the lost-love idyll that made him famous; the model German Novelle. No PD English translation; staged in German. [Translation: German original (no PD English translation).]

title: The Sonnets, Triumphs, and Other Poems of Petrarch
creator: Francesco Petrarca
description: The complete Canzoniere, Triumphs, and other poems in the first complete English verse rendering (various translators, Bell's Illustrated Library, 1879): the lyric sequence that invented the sonnet and founded Renaissance European poetry.

title: Jerusalem Delivered
creator: Torquato Tasso
description: Tasso's epic of the First Crusade in Edward Fairfax's 1600 English translation — itself a landmark of English Renaissance literature, read by Milton and Dryden.

title: The Poems of Giacomo Leopardi
creator: Giacomo Leopardi
description: The complete lyric poetry of Italy's great Romantic pessimist in Frederick Townsend's 1887 translation. Leopardi's prose dialogues are staged separately; this is the Canti.

title: The House by the Medlar-Tree (I Malavoglia)
creator: Giovanni Verga
description: The foundational novel of Italian verismo in Mary A. Craig's 1890 translation (with W. D. Howells's introduction): the tragedy of the Malavoglia fishing family.

title: Confessions of Zeno
creator: Italo Svevo
description: Svevo's 1923 modernist masterpiece in Beryl de Zoete's original 1930 English translation (Knopf): the psychoanalytic memoirs of Zeno Cosini, championed by James Joyce.

title: The Art of Worldly Wisdom
creator: Baltasar Gracián
description: Gracián's Oráculo manual (1647) — 300 maxims on prudence, power, and self-mastery, which Schopenhauer translated himself and called 'absolutely unique' — in Joseph Jacobs's 1892 English rendering.

title: The Wonder-Working Magician
creator: Pedro Calderón de la Barca
description: Calderón's great drama of the Faust theme — the legend of St. Cyprian — in MacCarthy's complete 1873 verse translation.

title: The Visions of Quevedo
creator: Francisco de Quevedo
description: Quevedo's Sueños — the most famous Spanish satire of the Golden Age — in Sir Roger L'Estrange's 1667 translation, itself a classic of Restoration English prose (this text follows the corrected 1668 third edition).

title: Trafalgar
creator: Benito Pérez Galdós
description: First volume of Galdós's Episodios Nacionales, the 46-novel chronicle of 19th-century Spain, in Clara Bell's 1884 translation: the Battle of Trafalgar through the boy narrator Gabriel Araceli.

title: La Regenta
creator: Leopoldo Alas
description: The greatest Spanish novel of the 19th century: Ana Ozores's tragedy in provincial Vetusta. Staged in the Spanish original — no public-domain English translation is known to exist.

title: Tragic Sense of Life
creator: Miguel de Unamuno
description: Unamuno's 1913 philosophical masterwork on the tragic conflict between reason and faith in J. E. Crawford Flitch's landmark 1921 English translation (Macmillan).

title: The Quest (La busca)
creator: Pío Baroja
description: First volume of Baroja's 'La lucha por la vida' trilogy in Isaac Goldberg's 1922 translation (Knopf): Manuel Alcázar's descent through Madrid's underworld — the novel Hemingway called his master.

title: Poesías completas
creator: Antonio Machado
description: The complete poetry of Spain's greatest 20th-century lyric poet — Soledades, Campos de Castilla, and the later poems. Staged in Spanish — no public-domain English translation is known to exist.

title: Os Maias
creator: Eça de Queirós
description: Portugal's greatest novel: the decline of the Maia family, the masterpiece of Portuguese realism. Staged in the Portuguese original — Aubrey Bell's 1925 English translation is public domain but no obtainable full text could be found.

title: The Improvisatore; or, Life in Italy
creator: Hans Christian Andersen
description: Andersen's breakthrough 1835 novel — the Roman artist's-life romance that made him famous across Europe before the fairy tales — in Mary Howitt's translation (Bentley 1847). Distinct from Andersen's Fairy Tales.

title: Arne; Early Tales and Sketches
creator: Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson
description: The peasant tales of Norway's Nobel laureate — 'Arne' and the early sketches that founded modern Norwegian literature — in Rasmus B. Anderson's classic translation (Houghton Mifflin, 1881–82).

title: The Family at Gilje
creator: Jonas Lie
description: Jonas Lie's beloved domestic novel of a Norwegian officer's family in the 1840s, translated by Samuel Coffin Eastman for the American-Scandinavian Foundation's Scandinavian Classics (1920).

title: Garman and Worse
creator: Alexander Lange Kielland
description: The sharpest satire of Norway's 'Great Four': a merchant dynasty's decline and the hypocrisies of church and capital, in W. W. Kettlewell's authorized 1885 English translation.

title: Pan
creator: Knut Hamsun
description: Hamsun's lyrical 1894 novel of Lieutenant Glahn's wild summer in Nordland — the nature-mysticism masterpiece of the Nobel laureate — in W. W. Worster's classic Knopf translation (1921). Distinct from Hunger and Growth of the Soil.

title: The Dramas of Aeschylus
creator: Aeschylus; Anna Swanwick (trans.)
description: The complete surviving Aeschylus — all seven tragedies (Agamemnon, Choephori, Eumenides, Persians, Seven Against Thebes, Prometheus Bound, Suppliants) in Anna Swanwick's celebrated verse translation, 4th revised edition 1886; metrically and stylistically distinct from the Blackie translation already in the library. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/dramasswa00aescuoft).

title: The Plays of Sophocles
creator: Sophocles; Robert Whitelaw (trans.)
description: All seven surviving plays of Sophocles (Ajax, Antigone, Electra, Oedipus the King, Oedipus at Colonus, Philoctetes, Trachiniae) in Robert Whitelaw's 1883 English verse translation; the standard Victorian verse rendering, complementing the Campbell prose translation already in the library. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/sophoclestransla00sophuoft).

title: Euripides, Vol. I (Way)
creator: Euripides; Arthur S. Way (trans.)
description: Volume I of the complete Loeb Euripides (first printed 1912; this scan a 1930 reprint): Iphigenia at Aulis, Rhesus, Hecuba, The Daughters of Troy (Trojan Women), Helen, in Arthur S. Way's verse translation — the only complete pre-1931 English verse Euripides; complements the selective Murray translations already in the library. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/euripideswitheng01euri).

title: Euripides, Vol. II (Way)
creator: Euripides; Arthur S. Way (trans.)
description: Volume II of the complete Loeb Euripides (first printed 1912; this scan a 1929 reprint): Electra, Orestes, Iphigenia in Taurica, Andromache, Cyclops, in Arthur S. Way's verse translation. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/euripideswitheng02euri).

title: Euripides, Vol. III (Way)
creator: Euripides; Arthur S. Way (trans.)
description: Volume III of the complete Loeb Euripides (first printed 1912; this scan a 1930 reprint): Bacchanals (Bacchae), Madness of Hercules (Heracles), Children of Hercules, Phoenician Maidens, Suppliants, in Arthur S. Way's verse translation. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/euripideswitheng03euri).

title: Euripides, Vol. IV (Way)
creator: Euripides; Arthur S. Way (trans.)
description: Volume IV of the complete Loeb Euripides (first printed 1912; this scan a 1928 reprint): Ion, Hippolytus, Medea, Alcestis, in Arthur S. Way's verse translation. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/euripideswitheng04euri).

title: Aristophanes, Vol. I (Rogers)
creator: Aristophanes; Benjamin Bickley Rogers (trans.)
description: Volume I of the complete Loeb Aristophanes (1924): The Acharnians, The Knights, The Clouds, The Wasps, in Benjamin Bickley Rogers's verse translation — the classic English verse rendering, complementing the anonymous prose Eleven Comedies already in the library. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/aristophaneswith01arisuoft).

title: Aristophanes, Vol. II (Rogers)
creator: Aristophanes; Benjamin Bickley Rogers (trans.)
description: Volume II of the complete Loeb Aristophanes (1924): The Peace, The Birds, The Frogs, in Benjamin Bickley Rogers's verse translation. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/AristophanesVolIi).

title: Aristophanes, Vol. III (Rogers)
creator: Aristophanes; Benjamin Bickley Rogers (trans.)
description: Volume III of the complete Loeb Aristophanes (1924): Lysistrata, Thesmophoriazusae, Ecclesiazusae, Plutus, in Benjamin Bickley Rogers's verse translation. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/aristophaneswith03arisuoft).

title: Menander: The Principal Fragments (Allinson)
creator: Menander; Francis G. Allinson (trans.)
description: Honestly-labeled fragments: the principal surviving fragments of Menander — the master of Greek New Comedy, whose work survives only in fragments and quotations — with facing Greek text, in Francis G. Allinson's Loeb translation (1921). Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/menanderprincipa00menauoft).

title: The Comedies of Plautus, Vol. I (Riley)
creator: Plautus; Henry Thomas Riley (trans.)
description: Volume I of Henry Thomas Riley's complete Bohn prose translation (1852): Trinummus, Miles Gloriosus, Bacchides, Stichus, Pseudolus, Menaechmi, Aulularia, Captivi, Asinaria, Curculio. Together with Vol. II this completes the surviving Plautus corpus in Riley's translation, superseding the two-play Riley selection already in the library. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/comediesplautus03plaugoog).

title: The Comedies of Plautus, Vol. II (Riley)
creator: Plautus; Henry Thomas Riley (trans.)
description: Volume II of Henry Thomas Riley's complete Bohn prose translation (1852): Amphitryon, Mercator, Cistellaria, Truculentus, Persa, Casina, Poenulus, Epidicus, Mostellaria, plus the fragments — completing the surviving Plautus corpus in Riley's translation. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/comediesliterall00plauuoft).

title: Terence, Vol. I (Sargeaunt)
creator: Terence; John Sargeaunt (trans.)
description: Volume I of the complete Loeb Terence (1912): The Lady of Andros, The Self-Tormentor, The Eunuch, in John Sargeaunt's translation with facing Latin text — the standard English edition of Rome's great comic playwright. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/terence000ijohn).

title: Terence, Vol. II (Sargeaunt)
creator: Terence; John Sargeaunt (trans.)
description: Volume II of the complete Loeb Terence (1912): Phormio, The Mother-in-Law (Hecyra), The Brothers (Adelphoe), in John Sargeaunt's translation with facing Latin text. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/terence00iijohn).

title: Seneca's Tragedies, Vol. I (Miller)
creator: Seneca; Frank Justus Miller (trans.)
description: Volume I of the complete Loeb Seneca tragedies (first printed 1917): Hercules Furens, Troades, Medea, Hippolytus (Phaedra), Oedipus, in Frank Justus Miller's translation — the Roman tragedies that shaped Renaissance and Elizabethan drama. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/tragedieswitheng01seneuoft).

title: Seneca's Tragedies, Vol. II (Miller)
creator: Seneca; Frank Justus Miller (trans.)
description: Volume II of the complete Loeb Seneca tragedies (first printed 1917; this scan a 1929 reprint): Agamemnon, Thyestes, Hercules Oetaeus, Phoenissae, Octavia, in Frank Justus Miller's translation. description: Tome 2 of the Muqaddimah — Ibn Khaldun's 14th-century pioneering treatise on history, society, and civilization — in Baron William MacGuckin de Slane's complete French translation (Notices et extraits des manuscrits, 1863-68), the standard scholarly French edition. Public domain. Sourced from French Wikisource (https://fr.wikisource.org/wiki/Livre:Ibn_Khaldoun_-_Prol%C3%A9gom%C3%A8nes,_Slane,_1863,_tome_II.djvu).

title: Les Prolégomènes d’Ibn Khaldoun, Tome III
creator: Ibn Khaldun; William MacGuckin de Slane (trans.)
description: Tome 3 of the Muqaddimah — Ibn Khaldun's 14th-century pioneering treatise on history, society, and civilization — in Baron William MacGuckin de Slane's complete French translation (Notices et extraits des manuscrits, 1863-68), the standard scholarly French edition. Public domain. Sourced from Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/lesprolgomne03abdauoft).

title: Kabbala Denudata, Tome I (Latin)
creator: Christian Knorr von Rosenroth
description: In Latin. Tome I of the great 17th-century anthology of Kabbalistic texts in Latin translation — the principal vehicle by which Lurianic and Zoharic Kabbalah reached the Christian West, and the most-cited primary source for early modern Christian Kabbalah. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: Kabbala Denudata, Tome II (Latin)
creator: Christian Knorr von Rosenroth
description: In Latin. Tome II of Knorr von Rosenroth's anthology (1684): commentaries, the Siphra de Zeniutha with Luria's commentary, and related treatises. No public-domain English translation exists.

title: La Règle du Temple
creator: Henri de Curzon (editor)
description: In French. The standard critical edition of the Rule of the Knights Templar, established from the three medieval manuscripts (Paris, Rome, Dijon) for the Société de l'Histoire de France — the edition every modern history of the Order cites. The first complete English translation (1992) remains in copyright.

title: Textes et monuments figurés relatifs aux mystères de Mithra, Tome I
creator: Franz Cumont
description: In French. Tome I (critical introduction and collected texts) of Cumont's monumental corpus of Mithraic sources — the foundational reference work of Mithraic studies, gathering every known inscription and literary text. The library holds Cumont's 1903 English summary; this is the full scholarly corpus behind it.

title: Textes et monuments figurés relatifs aux mystères de Mithra, Tome II
creator: Franz Cumont
description: In French. Tome II of Cumont's Mithraic corpus: the monuments — 493 figures and 9 heliotype plates, catalogued and described — the archaeological companion to Tome I's texts.

title: The Seven Tablets of Creation, Vol. I
creator: L. W. King
description: The first complete English translation of the Enuma Elish (Babylonian creation epic), with introduction, transliterations, and commentary — the edition that introduced the Babylonian Genesis to the English-speaking world. Vol. I: introduction and English translations.

title: The Seven Tablets of Creation, Vol. II: Supplementary Texts
creator: L. W. King
description: Vol. II of King's edition: newly published Neo-Babylonian cuneiform texts of the Creation series (autographed plates) with English preface and tablet descriptions.

title: The Epic of Gilgamish
creator: R. Campbell Thompson (translator)
description: A scholarly verse translation of the Gilgamesh epic in English hexameters, from a fresh collation of the British Museum cuneiform tablets — the standard interwar English Gilgamesh. (Thompson spells the hero 'Gilgamish' throughout.)

title: Lectures on the Origin and Growth of Religion as Illustrated by the Religion of the Ancient Babylonians
creator: A. H. Sayce
description: Sayce's 1887 Hibbert Lectures — the founding English statement of Assyriology's bearing on the history of religion, enormously cited in its day.

title: Essays on the Sacred Language, Writings, and Religion of the Parsis
creator: Martin Haug (edited and enlarged by E. W. West)
description: Haug's foundational essays on the Zoroastrian scriptures — the work that established Pahlavi studies and the scholarly study of the Avesta in the West, with his outline of a Pahlavi-Pazand glossary. The single most-cited 19th-century work on the Parsi religion.

title: Aus Sibirien: Lose Blätter aus meinem Tagebuche, Erster Band
creator: Wilhelm Radloff
description: In German. Vol. I of Radloff's Siberian travel journals (1859-1870) — among the earliest first-hand European accounts of Siberian shamanism, with detailed descriptions of shamanic séances, spirit beliefs, and the Turkic peoples of the Altai.

title: Aus Sibirien: Lose Blätter aus meinem Tagebuche, Zweiter Band
creator: Wilhelm Radloff
description: In German. Vol. II of Radloff's Siberian journals — further shamanic and ethnographic material from the Altai and the Kirghiz steppe, closing with his table of Russian measures.

title: The Threshold of Religion
creator: R. R. Marett
description: Marett's landmark challenge to Tylor's animism — arguing that 'mana'-like pre-animistic awe, not belief in spirits, stands at the threshold of religion. The founding text of the mana-taboo school of early anthropology of religion.

title: Reincarnation: A Study of Forgotten Truth
creator: E. D. Walker
description: The first systematic English survey of reincarnation beliefs across world religions — Hindu, Buddhist, Greek, early Christian, and modern — the book that introduced the doctrine to the late-19th-century Anglophone public and remained the standard reference for decades.

title: One Hundred Proofs That the Earth Is Not a Globe
creator: William Carpenter
description: The most-circulated flat-earth tract of the 19th century — one hundred numbered 'proofs' of a flat, stationary earth, endlessly reprinted by flat-earth societies into the present. The key primary text of the flat-earth cell.

title: Lectures on Homoeopathic Materia Medica
creator: James Tyler Kent
source: Internet Archive (in.ernet.dli.2015.458552), Calcutta: Roy Publishing House, 1904 (1st ed.)
description: Kent's Lectures — the defining American homeopathic materia medica, remedy-by-remedy lectures delivered at the Post-Graduate School of Homoeopathics. All remedy lectures are complete (Abies through Zincum); the source scan lacks the final leaves of the printed index, which breaks off at 'Carbo veg.'

title: Materia Medica Pura, Vol. I
creator: Samuel Hahnemann (translated by R. E. Dudgeon, with annotations by Richard Hughes)
source: Internet Archive (b28121612_0002), London: Hahnemann Publishing Society, 1880
description: Vol. I of Dudgeon's English translation of Hahnemann's Materia Medica Pura — the foundational provings of homeopathy, remedy by remedy. The translation that carried Hahnemann's pure materia medica into English.

title: Materia Medica Pura, Vol. II
creator: Samuel Hahnemann (translated by R. E. Dudgeon, with annotations by Richard Hughes)
source: Internet Archive (b28121612_0001), London: Hahnemann Publishing Society, 1881
description: Vol. II of Dudgeon's English translation of Hahnemann's Materia Medica Pura (Ledum through Verbascum), completing the two-volume English edition.

title: Project Grudge Report: Unidentified Flying Objects (August 1949)
creator: U.S. Air Force, Air Materiel Command
source: Internet Archive (project-grudge-august-1949-part-1..8), declassified U.S. government report
description: The complete declassified Project Grudge final report (August 1949) — the U.S. Air Force's second official UFO investigation, successor to Project Sign and predecessor to Project Blue Book. Assembled here from the eight separately-hosted report parts. A pivotal primary document of the early UFO era.

title: Plutarch's Lives, Vol. I (Langhorne, 1813)
creator: Plutarch (John & William Langhorne, trans.)
description: Langhorne's Plutarch's Lives, Vol. 1 (Wrangham 2nd ed., 1813): Life of Plutarch, Theseus, Romulus, Lycurgus, Numa, Solon, Publicola, Themistocles, Camillus. Completes the 6-volume set — Vol. 1 was the missing volume.

title: The Mathnawí of Jalálu'ddín Rūmí, Vol. II (Nicholson)
creator: Jalál al-Dîn Rūmí (R. A. Nicholson, trans.)
description: Nicholson's Mathnawi, Vol. 2 (1926): the English translation of Books I–II (E.J.W. Gibb Memorial, New Series IV.2). Completes the pre-1931 set's missing volume; Vols. 5–8 with batch 07.

title: The Sacred Magic of Abramelin the Mage (Book 3)
creator: Abraham of Worms (S. L. MacGregor Mathers, trans.)
description: The Third Book of the Sacred Magic (Mathers 1900, Rowe typeset): the magic squares — the operative core of the Abramelin system. Completes the three-book set; Books 1–2 already live.

title: Kalevala, Volume II (of 2): The Land of the Heroes
creator: Elias Lönnrot (W. F. Kirby, trans.)
description: Kalevala, Vol. 2 (Kirby trans., 1907): Runos 26–50 — Kullervo, the Sampo cycle, and the closing runos. Completes the 2-volume Kirby set; the held 'Volume 2' is a different (Berserker) edition.

title: Sextus Empiricus, Vol. I: Outlines of Pyrrhonism (Bury, 1933)
creator: Sextus Empiricus (R. G. Bury, trans.)
description: The primary source for ancient Pyrrhonist skepticism: Bury's Loeb translation of the Outlines of Pyrrhonism (Books I–III) with his introduction on the dogmatic philosophies (Heinemann/Putnam, 1933). Public domain: no copyright renewal found in the Stanford Copyright Renewal Database (renewal window 1960–61).

title: The Book of Chilam Balam of Chumayel
creator: Ralph L. Roys (trans. and ed.)
description: The most important of the Books of Chilam Balam — the core native Maya literary-historical source for colonial Yucatan, in Roys' translation (Carnegie Institution of Washington, 1933). Public domain: no copyright renewal (Stanford Copyright Renewal Database; source scan notes timely non-renewal). Note: the source scan excludes the edition's footnotes; the translated text is complete.

title: The Fragments of Zeno and Cleanthes
creator: Zeno of Citium and Cleanthes, trans. A. C. Pearson
description: The first English collection of the fragments of Zeno of Citium and Cleanthes, the founders of Stoicism — the only direct window onto early Stoic doctrine. A. C. Pearson’s 1891 Cambridge edition, with introduction and explanatory notes.

title: Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta, Vol. I: Zeno and His Disciples
creator: Hans von Arnim (editor)
description: Von Arnim’s Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta, vol. I: the complete fragments of Zeno of Citium and his immediate disciples in Greek and Latin — the foundational source-book for early Stoicism.

title: Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta, Vol. II: Chrysippus on Logic and Physics
creator: Hans von Arnim (editor)
description: SVF vol. II: the fragments of Chrysippus on logic and physics, in Greek and Latin. Chrysippus was the Stoa’s great systematizer; most of what survives of him is gathered here.

title: Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta, Vol. III: Chrysippus on Ethics
creator: Hans von Arnim (editor)
description: SVF vol. III: the fragments of Chrysippus on ethics, with fragments of his successors, in Greek and Latin — the core of Stoic moral doctrine and its early transmission.

title: Stoicorum Veterum Fragmenta, Vol. IV: Indices
creator: Hans von Arnim (editor); indices by Maximilian Adler
description: SVF vol. IV: the general indices to von Arnim’s collection, compiled by Maximilian Adler — the key to navigating the fragments of the early Stoa (Greek and Latin).

title: Stoic and Epicurean
creator: R. D. Hicks
description: R. D. Hicks’s 1910 survey Stoic and Epicurean — the classic English introduction to the two great Hellenistic schools: their physics, logic, ethics, and religious thought.

title: Epicurus: The Extant Remains
creator: Epicurus, ed. and trans. Cyril Bailey
description: Cyril Bailey’s 1926 Oxford edition of Epicurus: the letters to Herodotus, Pythocles, and Menoeceus, the Principal Doctrines, the Vatican Sayings, and the fragments — with translation, critical apparatus, and notes. The standard English Epicurus of its era.

title: The Greek Atomists and Epicurus: A Study
creator: Cyril Bailey
description: Cyril Bailey’s 1928 study The Greek Atomists and Epicurus — the landmark English account of ancient atomism from Leucippus and Democritus through Epicurus to Lucretius.

title: The Fragments of the Work of Heraclitus of Ephesus on Nature
creator: Heraclitus, trans. G. T. W. Patrick
description: G. T. W. Patrick’s 1889 English translation of the fragments of Heraclitus of Ephesus on Nature, from Bywater’s Greek text, with historical and critical introduction — the first standalone English Heraclitus.

title: The Characters of Theophrastus
creator: Theophrastus, trans. R. C. Jebb
description: R. C. Jebb’s 1870 edition of Theophrastus’s Characters — the thirty sketches of human types, with English translation, introduction, and notes. The founding text of character-writing and a key witness to Athenian daily life.

title: Epictetus His Morals, with Simplicius His Comment
creator: Epictetus and Simplicius, trans. George Stanhope
description: George Stanhope’s English version of Epictetus’s Enchiridion with the commentary of Simplicius (5th edition, 1741; first published 1694), with the Life of Epictetus from Boileau — the only pre-modern English Simplicius, and the form in which generations of English readers met Stoic ethics.

title: De Finibus Bonorum et Malorum (On Ends)
creator: Cicero, trans. H. Rackham
description: Cicero’s De Finibus Bonorum et Malorum in H. Rackham’s 1914 Loeb translation (Latin with facing English) — the fullest surviving Roman account of Epicurean, Stoic, and Academic ethics, in five books.

title: The Works of the Emperor Julian, Vol. I
creator: Julian (Emperor), trans. Wilmer Cave Wright
description: The Works of the Emperor Julian, vol. I (Loeb Classical Library, trans. Wilmer Cave Wright, 1913): Orations 1–5, Greek with facing English — the pagan emperor’s philosophical orations.

title: The Works of the Emperor Julian, Vol. II
creator: Julian (Emperor), trans. Wilmer Cave Wright
description: The Works of the Emperor Julian, vol. II (Loeb, trans. Wilmer Cave Wright, 1913): Orations 6–8, fragments, and letters — including the Caesars and the Misopogon.

title: The Works of the Emperor Julian, Vol. III
creator: Julian (Emperor), trans. Wilmer Cave Wright
description: The Works of the Emperor Julian, vol. III (Loeb, trans. Wilmer Cave Wright, 1923): the letters and fragments, including Against the Galilaeans — Julian’s philosophical case against Christianity.

title: The Roman History of Appian of Alexandria, Vol. I: The Foreign Wars
creator: Appian (Horace White, trans.)
description: Appian's Roman History (c. 160 CE), Vol. I: the Foreign Wars — the Spanish, Hannibalic, Punic, Illyrian, Syrian and Mithridatic wars, with the surviving fragments of the lost books. The sole continuous narrative of Rome's conquest of the Mediterranean from the conquered peoples' advocate. Horace White's 1899 translation via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: The Roman History of Appian of Alexandria, Vol. II: The Civil Wars
creator: Appian (Horace White, trans.)
description: Appian's Roman History (c. 160 CE), Vol. II: the Civil Wars, Books I-V — the Gracchi to Sextus Pompeius. The only continuous ancient narrative of the Roman civil wars, our fullest source for the fall of the Republic. With index. Horace White's 1899 translation via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: Aurelius Victor: Historia Romana (1871 Tauchnitz Latin edition)
creator: Sextus Aurelius Victor
description: Sextus Aurelius Victor's Historia Romana (c. 361 CE): the De Caesaribus — imperial biographies from Augustus to Constantius II — with the Origo Gentis Romanae, De Viris Illustribus, and Epitome de Caesaribus. The 4th-century breviarium tradition's key witness. No PD English translation exists; 1871 Tauchnitz Latin edition via Internet Archive.

title: Chaldæan Fragments, chiefly from Berossus (Cory, 1832)
creator: Berossus (Isaac Preston Cory, trans.)
description: The surviving fragments of Berossus's Babyloniaca (c. 280 BCE) with the allied Chaldæan fragments (Abydenus, Megasthenes, Alexander Polyhistor): the cosmogony, the deluge, the antediluvian kings, Nebuchadnezzar, and the fall of Babylon — the Babylonian priest's own account, our key native source for Mesopotamian chronology. From Cory's Ancient Fragments (1832) via Internet Archive (English text only).

title: Lives of Eminent Commanders
creator: Cornelius Nepos (Rev. John Selby Watson, trans.)
description: Cornelius Nepos's Lives (c. 40 BCE) — the first Latin biographical collection: Miltiades, Themistocles, Aristides, Epaminondas, Hannibal, Cato, Atticus and the other Greek and Carthaginian commanders. The biographical model for the whole Roman tradition. With Watson's biographical notice. Rev. John Selby Watson's 1853 translation via Internet Archive.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 1: Books I-XI (Fragments)
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), fragments of Books 1-11, from the foundation of Rome through the Punic Wars, preserved in Byzantine excerpts, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 2: Books XII-XXXV (Fragments)
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), fragments of Books 12-35, the conquest of the Mediterranean world, preserved in Byzantine excerpts, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 3: Books XXXVI-XL
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), Books 36-40: Pompey, the conspiracy of Catiline, Caesar in Gaul, and the outbreak of the Civil War, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 4: Books XLI-XLV
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), Books 41-45: the Civil War, Caesar's dictatorship, and his assassination, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 5: Books XLVI-L
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), Books 46-50: the Second Triumvirate, Philippi, and the rise of Octavian, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 6: Books LI-LV
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), Books 51-55: Actium, the Augustan settlement, and the early Principate, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 7: Books LVI-LX
creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), Books 56-60: Tiberius, Caligula, and Claudius, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only).
