creator: Samuel Hahnemann
description: Hahnemann's The Chronic Diseases, vol. V (Hempel translation, 1845) — the psora doctrine and the antipsoric materia medica: the second pillar of homeopathy beside the Organon.

title: The Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica, Vol. I
creator: Timothy Field Allen
description: T. F. Allen's Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica, vol. I (1874) — the exhaustive proving record: every symptom from every prover, arranged by remedy. The largest homeopathic materia medica ever compiled.

creator: Timothy Field Allen
description: T. F. Allen's Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica, vol. II (1874) — the exhaustive proving record: every symptom from every prover, arranged by remedy. The largest homeopathic materia medica ever compiled.

creator: Timothy Field Allen
description: T. F. Allen's Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica, vol. X (1879) — the exhaustive proving record: every symptom from every prover, arranged by remedy. The largest homeopathic materia medica ever compiled.

title: The Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica: Index
creator: Timothy Field Allen
description: The general index to T. F. Allen's Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica (1879) — the key to the ten volumes: every symptom and remedy cross-referenced.

title: Repertory of the Homoeopathic Materia Medica
creator: James Tyler Kent
description: James Tyler Kent's Repertory of the Homoeopathic Materia Medica (1897, first edition) — the repertory: symptoms arranged by rubric with remedy gradings, the finding tool of the Kentian school and the most influential repertory in homeopathy.

title: The American Practice of Medicine, Vol. I
creator: Wooster Beach
description: Wooster Beach's The American Practice of Medicine, vol. I (1833) — the eclectic school's founding textbook: botanic practice against the heroic medicine of bleeding and calomel.

title: The American Practice of Medicine, Vol. II
creator: Wooster Beach
description: Wooster Beach's The American Practice of Medicine, vol. II (1833) — the eclectic school's founding textbook: botanic practice against the heroic medicine of bleeding and calomel.

title: The American Practice of Medicine, Vol. III
creator: Wooster Beach
description: Wooster Beach's The American Practice of Medicine, vol. III (1833) — the eclectic school's founding textbook: botanic practice against the heroic medicine of bleeding and calomel.

title: The Condensed Materia Medica
creator: Constantine Hering
description: Constantine Hering's The Condensed Materia Medica (1884, second edition) — the compact Hering: the guiding symptoms condensed for the prescriber's pocket, the most portable form of the great materia medica.

title: Key-Notes and Characteristics with Comparisons of Some of the Leading Remedies of the Materia Medica
creator: Henry C. Allen
description: Henry C. Allen's Key-Notes and Characteristics (1899, second edition) — the keynote prescriber's classic: leading remedies with comparisons, the most reprinted homeopathic handbook of the 20th century.

title: New Guide to Health; or, Botanic Family Physician
creator: Samuel Thomson
description: Samuel Thomson's New Guide to Health; or, Botanic Family Physician (1822) — the Thomsonian system: steam, lobelia and cayenne against the mineral poisons of regular medicine. The book that launched America's first mass medical movement.

title: A Narrative of the Life and Medical Discoveries of Samuel Thomson
creator: Samuel Thomson
description: Samuel Thomson's Narrative of the Life and Medical Discoveries (1829) — the founder's own story: the New Hampshire farmer's path to the botanic system, the trials, the persecutions, the vindication.

title: Mundus Subterraneus (Latin)
creator: Athanasius Kircher
description: Athanasius Kircher's Mundus Subterraneus (1665) — the subterranean world: volcanoes, earthquakes, the central fire, in twelve books. The great baroque geology; staged in the Latin original as a documentary text (no public-domain English translation exists).

title: Lost Illusions
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Ellen Marriage
description: Balzac's great novel of ambition and journalism — Lucien de Rubempré's rise and ruin in Paris, the centerpiece of the Human Comedy's 'Scènes de la vie de province' and 'Scènes de la vie parisienne'. Ellen Marriage's 1895 Dent translation, complete in all three parts.

title: The Magic Skin
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Ellen Marriage
description: La Peau de chagrin — the Faustian talisman novel that made Balzac famous: a magic ass's skin grants every wish while shrinking with each desire. The philosophical cornerstone of the Human Comedy. Ellen Marriage's 1895 translation.

title: The Rise and Fall of César Birotteau
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Katharine Prescott Wormeley
description: Balzac's great bourgeois tragedy — the rise and bankruptcy of a Parisian perfumer, the Human Comedy's definitive study of commerce, credit, and speculation. Katharine Prescott Wormeley's Roberts Brothers translation.

title: The Country Doctor
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Ellen Marriage and Clara Bell
description: Le Médecin de campagne — Balzac's utopian counterpoint to his Paris novels: a doctor's regeneration of a Savoy village, the Human Comedy's most philosophical provincial novel. Ellen Marriage/Clara Bell translation.

title: Cousin Pons
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Ellen Marriage
description: The second half of Balzac's 'Les Parents pauvres' diptych with Cousin Bette — the musician Pons, his art collection, and the vultures who circle it; among the darkest of the late Human Comedy novels. Ellen Marriage's translation.

title: Scenes from a Courtesan's Life
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. James Waring
description: Splendeurs et misères des courtisanes (A Harlot High and Low) — Balzac's vast criminal-underworld sequel to Lost Illusions: Esther, Nucingen, and Vautrin's return. James Waring's 1898 translation.

title: Catherine de Medici
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Katharine Prescott Wormeley
description: Balzac's historical-philosophical study of Catherine de' Medici — the Human Comedy's 'Philosophical Studies' defense of the much-maligned queen, blending history and political theory. Wormeley's translation.

title: Colonel Chabert
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Ellen Marriage and Clara Bell
description: Balzac's perfect novella — a Napoleonic officer left for dead at Eylau returns to find his wife remarried and the law unwilling to resurrect him. The Human Comedy in miniature. Marriage/Bell translation.

title: The Physiology of Marriage
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Katharine Prescott Wormeley
description: Balzac's sardonic analytical treatise on marriage — part physiology, part satire, the book that first made his name in 1829 and the founding text of his 'Analytic Studies'. Wormeley's translation.

title: The Thirteen
creator: Honoré de Balzac, trans. Katharine Prescott Wormeley and Ellen Marriage
description: Histoire des Treize — Balzac's trilogy of the secret society of thirteen powerful men (Ferragus, The Duchess of Langeais, The Girl with the Golden Eyes); the Human Comedy's conspiratorial Paris. Wormeley/Marriage translations.

title: Sentimental Education
creator: Gustave Flaubert, trans. M. Walter Dunne edition translation
description: L'Éducation sentimentale — Flaubert's novel of 1848: Frédéric Moreau's passive drift through revolution, love, and disillusion, the great anti-Bildungsroman of French realism. Complete in both volumes, Dunne 1904 translation.

title: The Temptation of Saint Anthony
creator: Gustave Flaubert, trans. Lafcadio Hearn
description: Flaubert's lifelong phantasmagoria — Saint Anthony's night of visions in the Egyptian desert, the book he called his life's work, rendered by Lafcadio Hearn with Odilon Redon illustrations noted in the edition.

title: Bouvard and Pécuchet
creator: Gustave Flaubert, trans. M. Walter Dunne edition translation
description: Flaubert's unfinished black comedy of human stupidity — two copyists retire to the country and fail at every science in turn; the great satire of bourgeois knowledge. Complete in both parts, Dunne 1904 translation.

title: On Love
creator: Stendhal, trans. Philip Sidney Woolf and Cecil N. Sidney Woolf
description: De l'amour — Stendhal's famous treatise on the psychology of love, origin of 'crystallization'; the essay that made him the inventor of the psychological novel's theory as well as its practice. Woolf translation, 1915.

title: The Charterhouse of Parma
creator: Stendhal, trans. C. K. Scott Moncrieff
description: La Chartreuse de Parme — Stendhal's Napoleonic masterpiece: Fabrice del Dongo, the Battle of Waterloo, and court intrigue at Parma; Balzac called it the century's greatest novel. Scott Moncrieff's translation, complete in two volumes, with Balzac's 'Study of M. Beyle' and Stendhal's reply.

title: Voltaire's Romances (Complete)
creator: Voltaire
description: The complete romances — Zadig, The Ingenu, The White Bull, Jeannot and Colin, and the other contes philosophiques in the classic 19th-century English renderings; Voltaire's fiction as Enlightenment weapon. Eckler 1889 edition.

title: A Philosophical Dictionary
creator: Voltaire, trans. William F. Fleming
description: The Dictionnaire philosophique complete — Voltaire's alphabetical arsenal against superstition and intolerance, the Enlightenment's most quotable reference work, in William F. Fleming's 1901 DuMont translation. All ten volumes merged.

title: History of Charles XII, King of Sweden
creator: Voltaire, trans. Winifred Todhunter
description: Voltaire's pioneering modern history — the meteoric life of Charles XII of Sweden, the book that made 'philosophical history' a genre and Voltaire a historian. Todhunter's Everyman translation.

title: The History of Peter the Great, Emperor of Russia
creator: Voltaire, trans. Tobias Smollett
description: Voltaire's history of Russia under Peter the Great, in Tobias Smollett's 1763 English translation — Enlightenment historiography by two of the century's sharpest pens. From the Samuel Johnson & Son 'English Classics' reprint.

title: Letters on England
creator: Voltaire
description: The Lettres philosophiques — Voltaire's 1734 letters from English exile that introduced Newton, Locke, and English liberty to France; the founding document of the French Enlightenment. Cassell's 1894 Morley edition.

title: Julie; or, The New Eloisa
creator: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, trans. William Kenrick
description: Julie, ou la nouvelle Héloïse — Rousseau's bestselling epistolary novel, the book that taught Europe to feel; the founding text of Romanticism in fiction. William Kenrick's 1761 first English translation ('Eloisa').

title: Émile; or, On Education
creator: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, trans. Barbara Foxley
description: Rousseau's treatise-novel on education — the natural upbringing of Émile, including the 'Profession of Faith of the Savoyard Vicar'; condemned on publication, foundational to modern educational thought. Barbara Foxley's Everyman translation.

title: Athaliah
creator: Jean Racine, trans. J. Donkersley
description: Athalie — Racine's last and most sacred tragedy, the biblical drama of Joash and the high priest Jehoiada, rendered in English blank verse by J. Donkersley (1873). Completes the library's Racine tragedies in English.

title: Polyeucte
creator: Pierre Corneille, trans. Thomas Constable
description: Corneille's Christian tragedy of the Armenian martyr Polyeuctus — the summit of French classical tragedy's religious strain, in Thomas Constable's Harvard Classics translation. Joins the library's Le Cid.

title: The Fables of La Fontaine (Complete)
creator: Jean de La Fontaine, trans. Walter Thornbury
description: The complete Fables in English verse — all twelve books, from 'The Grasshopper and the Ant' to the closing apologue, in Walter Thornbury's verse translation; the book that made the fable a French art form.

title: Pan Michael
creator: Henryk Sienkiewicz, trans. Jeremiah Curtin
description: Pan Wołodyjowski — the closing volume of Sienkiewicz's Trilogy: the little knight's last stand at Kamieniec against the Turks, completing With Fire and Sword and The Deluge. Jeremiah Curtin's 1893 translation.

title: The Steel Flea
creator: Nikolai Leskov, trans. Isabel Florence Hapgood
description: Levsha — Leskov's beloved skaz tale of the Tula gunsmith who shoes the English steel flea; the great fable of Russian craft versus Western mechanism. Isabel Hapgood's 1890 translation.

title: Journal of Discourses, Vol. I
creator: Brigham Young, et al.
description: Volume I of the Journal of Discourses (Liverpool, 1854): stenographic reports of sermons by Brigham Young, his counsellors, the Twelve Apostles and others — the running doctrinal record of 19th-century Mormonism.

creator: Brigham Young, et al.
description: Volume XXVI of the Journal of Discourses (Liverpool, 1886): stenographic reports of sermons by Brigham Young, his counsellors, the Twelve Apostles and others — the running doctrinal record of 19th-century Mormonism.

title: Doctrine and Covenants of the Church of the Latter Day Saints (1835)
creator: Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, Sidney Rigdon, Frederick G. Williams
description: The 1835 Kirtland first edition of the Doctrine and Covenants — the foundational Mormon book of revelations, including the Lectures on Faith (later removed) and the 1835 revelations. The founding doctrinal text of the Latter Day Saint movement.

title: The Pearl of Great Price (1851)
creator: Joseph Smith
description: The 1851 Liverpool first edition of the Pearl of Great Price (Franklin D. Richards): the founding pamphlet-selection of Mormon scripture — Book of Moses extracts, Book of Abraham, Joseph Smith history, Articles of Faith. One of Mormonism's four standard works in embryo.

title: Testimony of Christ's Second Appearing
creator: United Society of Believers (Shakers)
description: The Shakers' foundational doctrinal exposition (2nd ed., 1810; 1st ed. 1808): the United Society of Believers' systematic testimony of Mother Ann Lee's mission, celibacy, communalism and the second appearing of Christ. The charter theology of American Shakerism.

title: Millennial Praises
creator: United Society of Believers (Shakers)
description: Millennial Praises (Hancock, 1813): the first Shaker hymnbook — 140+ hymns codifying Shaker worship, dance-song and theology in verse. The movement's liturgical and devotional core.

title: Testimonies of the Life, Character, Revelations and Doctrines of Mother Ann Lee
creator: United Society of Believers (Shakers)
description: Testimonies concerning Mother Ann Lee and the elders (text first written 1816; this scan the 1888 reprint): first-hand witness accounts of the Shaker foundress — the movement's primary hagiographical and doctrinal source.

title: Chronicon Ephratense: A History of the Community of Seventh Day Baptists at Ephrata
creator: Lamech and Agrippa (Brotherhood of Ephrata), trans. J. Max Hark
description: J. Max Hark's 1889 English translation of the Chronicon Ephratense (orig. German, Ephrata, 1786): the insider chronicle of the Ephrata Cloister — Conrad Beissel's celibate communistic Seventh-Day Baptist community, its mysticism, music and printing press. The primary document of America's most famous Pietist commune.

title: History of American Socialisms
creator: John Humphrey Noyes
description: John Humphrey Noyes's History of American Socialisms (1870): the Oneida founder's documentary history of America's utopian communes — Shakers, Owenites, Fourierists, Oneida itself — written from inside the movement. The primary source on 19th-century American communalism.

title: The Quimby Manuscripts
creator: Phineas Parkhurst Quimby, ed. Horatio W. Dresser
description: Horatio Dresser's 1921 edition of the Quimby Manuscripts: the writings of Phineas P. Quimby (1802–1866), the mental-healing pioneer whose ideas seeded New Thought and Christian Science — the movement's acknowledged source text, published from his manuscripts.

title: Scientific Christian Mental Practice
creator: Emma Curtis Hopkins
description: Emma Curtis Hopkins's Scientific Christian Mental Practice (1888): the textbook of the 'teacher of teachers' — the systematic New Thought course (Statement of Being, denials and affirmations) that trained Charles Fillmore, the Cadys and a generation of New Thought ministers.

title: The Science of Getting Rich
creator: Wallace D. Wattles
description: Wallace Wattles's The Science of Getting Rich (1910): the New Thought prosperity classic — 'thinking in the Certain Way' — the single most cited prosperity text of the movement, source of a century of success literature.

title: The Science of Being Well
creator: Wallace D. Wattles
description: The Science of Being Well (1910): Wattles's New Thought health companion to The Science of Getting Rich — the mental-science approach to health.

title: The Science of Being Great
creator: Wallace D. Wattles
description: The Science of Being Great (1911): the third of Wattles's New Thought trilogy — greatness as the expression of the advancing mind; completes the Getting Rich / Being Well / Being Great set.

title: The Science of Mind
creator: Ernest Holmes
description: Ernest Holmes's The Science of Mind (1926 first edition): the founding textbook of Religious Science — the complete course of lessons in the Science of Mind and Spirit that launched the Religious Science movement.

title: A Traveller's Narrative Written to Illustrate the Episode of the Bab
creator: E. G. Browne (translator)
description: E. G. Browne's 1891 Cambridge edition of the Babi history attributed to 'Abdu'l-Baha — the foundational Western documentary source on the Bab and the Babi movement, with Browne's introduction and notes. The primary English witness to 1844–1850 Babism.

title: Manual of The Mother Church
creator: Mary Baker Eddy
description: Mary Baker Eddy's Manual of The Mother Church (89th edition, 1903 printing): the by-laws and church government of Christian Science — the organizational charter of the movement, text fixed in Eddy's lifetime.

title: Retrospection and Introspection
creator: Mary Baker Eddy
description: Retrospection and Introspection (1891): Mary Baker Eddy's autobiographical account — her discovery of Christian Science, the break with Quimby, and the founding of the movement, in her own words.

title: Steps to Christ
creator: Ellen G. White
description: Ellen G. White's Steps to Christ (1892): the Adventist prophet's devotional classic — the most widely read Adventist book ever, the movement's spiritual handbook.

title: A Voice of Warning and Instruction to All People
creator: Parley P. Pratt
description: Parley P. Pratt's A Voice of Warning (8th ed., Liverpool, 1854; 1st ed. 1837): the classic early Mormon missionary apologetic — prophecy, the Book of Mormon, the kingdom of God. The most reprinted Mormon tract of the 19th century.

title: The Day of Vengeance (Studies in the Scriptures, Vol. 4)
creator: Charles Taze Russell
description: Studies in the Scriptures Vol. 4 (1897, first published as The Day of Vengeance): Russell's exposition of the 'battle of Armageddon' and the end of the Gentile times — the eschatological core of the Bible Student / Jehovah's Witness movement.

title: The At-One-Ment Between God and Man (Studies in the Scriptures, Vol. 5)
creator: Charles Taze Russell
description: Studies in the Scriptures Vol. 5 (1899): The At-One-Ment Between God and Man — Russell's systematic doctrine of the ransom and atonement, the theological center of the Studies series.

title: The New Creation (Studies in the Scriptures, Vol. 6)
creator: Charles Taze Russell
description: Studies in the Scriptures Vol. 6 (1904): The New Creation — Russell's ecclesiology and ethics: the calling, consecration and discipline of the 'new creature.' Completes Russell's own six-volume series.

title: The Finished Mystery (Studies in the Scriptures, Vol. 7)
creator: Charles Taze Russell (posthumous)
description: The Finished Mystery (1917): the posthumous Vol. 7 of Studies in the Scriptures — the verse-by-verse exposition of Revelation, Ezekiel and the Song of Solomon whose publication triggered the 1918 schism. Completes the seven-volume set.

title: Translation of Several Principal Books, Passages, and Texts of the Veds
creator: Rammohun Roy
description: Rammohun Roy's Translation of Several Principal Books, Passages, and Texts of the Veds (1832, 2nd ed.): the first Indian English renderings of Upanishadic/Vedantic texts — the founding document of Hindu reform and the Bengal Renaissance.

title: The Satyarth Prakash (Light of Truth)
creator: Dayananda Saraswati, trans. Durga Prasad
description: Durga Prasad's 1908 English translation of Dayananda Saraswati's Satyarth Prakash: the Arya Samaj founder's 'exposé of right sense' — Vedic reform, critique of idolatry and sectarianism. The charter text of modern Hindu reformism.

title: The Isha Upanishad
creator: Sri Aurobindo (trans. and commentary)
description: Sri Aurobindo's Isha Upanishad (2nd ed., Calcutta, 1924; 1st ed. 1921): his translation with analysis of the Upanishad — the seed of Integral Yoga's scriptural hermeneutics, from the Arya years.

title: The System of the Vedanta
creator: Paul Deussen, trans. Charles Johnston
description: Charles Johnston's 1912 English translation of Paul Deussen's System des Vedanta: the great German systematization of Shankara's Advaita from the Brahma-Sutras — the West's first rigorous Vedanta system, in the Schopenhauerian lineage.

title: The Nyaya Sutras of Gotama
creator: Gautama (attrib.), trans. Satis Chandra Vidyabhusana
description: Satis Chandra Vidyabhusana's 1913 English translation of the Nyaya Sutras (Sacred Books of the Hindus, vol. 8): the foundational text of Indian logic — the first complete English Nyaya Sutras.

title: The Markandeya Purana
creator: F. Eden Pargiter (translator)
description: F. Eden Pargiter's 1904 English translation of the Markandeya Purana (Bibliotheca Indica) — including the Devi Mahatmya, the great Goddess text. The standard scholarly English Markandeya Purana.

title: Miscellaneous Essays, Vol. I
creator: H. T. Colebrooke
description: H. T. Colebrooke's Miscellaneous Essays Vol. I (1837): the founding essays of British Indology — on the Vedas, Sanskrit grammar, Hindu law and astronomy. The field's charter collection.

title: Miscellaneous Essays, Vol. II
creator: H. T. Colebrooke
description: H. T. Colebrooke's Miscellaneous Essays Vol. II (1837): completing the two-volume set — further essays on Indian philosophy, mathematics and literature.

title: The Holy Science
creator: Swami Sri Yukteswar Giri
description: Swami Sri Yukteswar's The Holy Science (1894; Kaivalya Darshanam): Yogananda's guru's exposition of the yugas and the unity of Hindu and Christian scripture — the doctrinal bridge of modern Kriya Yoga.

title: Die Reden Gotamo Buddhos: Mittlere Sammlung, Erster Band
creator: Karl Eugen Neumann (translator)
description: Karl Eugen Neumann's German translation of the Majjhima Nikaya, Vol. 1 (Mittlere Sammlung): the pioneering complete German Pali canon translation — the foundation of German Buddhist studies. In German; no PD English exists.

title: Die Reden Gotamo Buddhos: Mittlere Sammlung, Zweiter Band
creator: Karl Eugen Neumann (translator)
description: Neumann's German Majjhima Nikaya, Vol. 2 (Mittlere Sammlung, Zweiter Band).

title: Die Reden Gotamo Buddhos: Mittlere Sammlung, Dritter Band
creator: Karl Eugen Neumann (translator)
description: Neumann's German Majjhima Nikaya, Vol. 3 (Mittlere Sammlung, Dritter Band) — completing the set.

title: The Buddha-Karita of Asvaghosha
creator: Asvaghosha, trans. E. B. Cowell
description: E. B. Cowell's 1893 English translation of Asvaghosha's Buddha-Karita (Anecdota Oxoniensia): the great 2nd-century Sanskrit life of the Buddha in English — the classical kavya biography, first translated complete.

title: Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet
creator: Sarat Chandra Das, ed. W. W. Rockhill
description: Sarat Chandra Das's Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet (1902, ed. Rockhill): the Bengali pandit-spy's narrative of his secret 1881–82 missions to Tibet — the primary Western documentary source on 19th-century Lhasa.

title: The Buddhism of Tibet, or Lamaism
creator: L. Austine Waddell
description: L. A. Waddell's The Buddhism of Tibet, or Lamaism (1895): the foundational Western study of Tibetan Buddhism — mystic cults, symbolism, mythology — from the Younghusband expedition's medical officer.

title: Three Years in Tibet
creator: Ekai Kawaguchi
description: Ekai Kawaguchi's Three Years in Tibet (1909): the Japanese monk's narrative of his disguised 1897–1903 sojourn in Tibet — the first Japanese account, a primary witness to pre-modern Lhasa.

title: A Dictionary of the Pali Language
creator: Robert Caesar Childers
description: Robert Caesar Childers's Dictionary of the Pali Language (1875): the first Pali dictionary — the lexicographical foundation of Pali studies and of all English translation of the Pali canon.

title: Of the Supreme Mysteries of Nature
creator: Paracelsus (Theophrastus von Hohenheim)
description: The famous 1656 Turner collection of Paracelsus in English: the spirits of the planets, occult philosophy, the magical cure of wounds and diseases, and the mysteries of the twelve signs of the zodiac — the key early-modern English Paracelsus.

title: A Ternary of Paradoxes
creator: Jan Baptista van Helmont (trans. Walter Charleton)
description: Van Helmont's three paradoxes in the landmark Charleton English edition: the magnetic cure of wounds, the nativity of tartar in wine, and the image of God in man — the foundational English text of Helmontian iatrochemistry.

title: The Works of the Highly Experienced and Famous Chymist, John Rudolph Glauber
creator: Johann Rudolf Glauber (trans. Christopher Packe)
description: The complete English Glauber in Packe's 1689 translation: new philosophical furnaces, the working of metallic mines and separation of metals, saltpetre, and the improvement of barren land — the great 17th-century chymical corpus in English.

title: Mr. William Lilly's History of His Life and Times
creator: William Lilly
description: The autobiography of England's most famous astrologer, written 1668-1681: Lilly's life from 1602, his astrological practice, the Civil War prophecies, and the world of 17th-century London astrology in his own words.

title: A Briefe Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres
creator: Claude Dariot (trans. Fabian Wither)
description: The earliest English astrology manual: Dariot's French introduction Englished in 1583, teaching the judgment of the stars, elections, and nativities — the seed of the English astrological tradition Lilly would inherit.

title: De astronomia tractatus X
creator: Guido Bonatti
description: Bonatti's complete Liber Astronomicus in the 1550 Basel Latin edition: the ten treatises on nativities, revolutions, elections, horary and mundane astrology — the great medieval Latin summa of judicial astrology in its original language.

title: Arcana arcanissima
creator: Michael Maier
description: Maier's mytho-alchemical masterwork: the most secret arcana decoded through Egyptian-Greek hieroglyphs and the fables of the golden age — the Rosicrucian physician's grand reading of mythology as chymical allegory, in Latin.

title: Septimana philosophica
creator: Michael Maier
description: Maier's philosophical week: golden enigmas on every kind of nature, framed as answers of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba — alchemy, nature-philosophy and emblematic wisdom in Latin.

title: De harmonia mundi totius
creator: Francesco Giorgi (Giorgio Veneto)
description: Giorgi's three canticles on the harmony of the whole world: Christian Kabbalah, the music of the spheres, and the concord of macrocosm and microcosm — the Franciscan friar's great Renaissance synthesis, in Latin.

title: Monde primitif, analysé et comparé avec le monde moderne, Tome VIII: Dissertations mêlées
creator: Antoine Court de Gébelin
description: The founding document of tarot history: volume 8 of Court de Gébelin's Monde primitif, containing the famous dissertation 'Du Jeu des Tarots' — the first claim of the tarot's Egyptian origin, with the six plates, in French.

title: Le Grand Etteilla, ou l'Art de tirer les cartes
creator: Etteilla (Jean-Baptiste Alliette)
description: Etteilla's art of card-reading: the first great system of tarot divination — meanings of the 78 cards, spreads, and the art of telling fortunes — in the 1850 French edition of the founder of cartomancy's work.

title: Crater Hermetis
creator: Lodovico Lazzarelli
description: Lazzarelli's Hermetic dialogue — Mercury instructs Tat on the Crater, the divine mixing-bowl of rebirth — printed with Ficino's Pimander and the Asclepius in Lefèvre's epochal 1505 Paris edition, in Latin.

title: Aucassin and Nicolete
creator: Anonymous (Andrew Lang, trans.)
description: The only surviving French chantefable (c. 1200), alternating prose and verse: the parodic love-story of Aucassin and the Saracen maid Nicolette. Andrew Lang’s classic 1887 translation, from the 1910 David Nutt edition.

title: The New Life (La Vita Nuova)
creator: Dante Alighieri (Dante Gabriel Rossetti, trans.)
description: Dante’s prosimetrum of his love for Beatrice (c. 1294) — the book that made Italian a literary language and the gateway to the Comedy. Rossetti’s poetic translation, Siddal edition.

title: Troilus and Criseyde
creator: Geoffrey Chaucer
description: Chaucer’s great tragic romance of Troilus and Criseyde at the siege of Troy (c. 1385) — his most finished poem and the summit of Middle English narrative verse.

title: The Vision and Creed of Piers Plowman, Vol. 1
creator: William Langland (Thomas Wright, ed.)
description: Langland’s alliterative dream-vision (c. 1370–86) — the greatest Middle English allegory of the search for the true Christian life. Thomas Wright’s standard edition, vol. 1.

title: The Vision and Creed of Piers Plowman, Vol. 2
creator: William Langland (Thomas Wright, ed.)
description: Langland’s alliterative dream-vision (c. 1370–86) — the greatest Middle English allegory of the search for the true Christian life. Thomas Wright’s standard edition, vol. 2.

title: Salámán and Absál
creator: Jami (Edward FitzGerald, trans.)
description: Jami’s Sufi allegory of the soul’s journey from earthly to divine love, in FitzGerald’s Miltonic verse (1856) — the companion-piece to his Rubáiyát. Extracted complete from the 1909 centenary edition.

title: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems
creator: Various (Arthur Waley, trans.)
description: Arthur Waley’s pioneering 1918 anthology that introduced classical Chinese poetry to English readers — from the Book of Songs to Po Chü-i, with his landmark introduction on Chinese verse.

title: The Poet Li Po, A.D. 701-762
creator: Li Bai (Arthur Waley, trans.)
description: Waley’s 1919 study and translations of Li Bai (701–762), the great Tang poet — the first substantial English Li Po, with biography and thirty poems.

title: The Story of Grettir the Strong
creator: Anonymous (Eiríkr Magnússon and William Morris, trans.)
description: The outlaw’s saga: Grettir the Strong’s nineteen years of defiance in medieval Iceland — the greatest of the Icelandic family sagas in outlaw form. Magnússon & Morris’s 1869 translation.

title: The Lay of the Cid
creator: Anonymous (R. Selden Rose and Leonard Bacon, trans.)
description: The oldest surviving Spanish epic (c. 1200): Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, the Cid, in exile and triumph during the Reconquista. Rose & Bacon’s 1919 verse translation.

title: Everyman, with Other Interludes, Including Eight Miracle Plays
creator: Anonymous (Ernest Rhys, ed.)
description: The Summoning of Everyman — the supreme English morality play (c. 1500) — with eight miracle plays including the Wakefield Second Shepherds’ Play and the Harrowing of Hell. Rhys’s Everyman’s Library edition.

title: Les Traditions Islamiques (El-Bokhâri), Tome I
creator: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bukhari (Octave Houdas and William Marçais, trans.)
description: The Sahih of al-Bukhari (d. 870) — the most authoritative Sunni hadith collection — in Houdas & Marçais’s complete French translation (Imprimerie nationale, 4 vols., 1903–1914), Tome I.

title: Les Traditions Islamiques (El-Bokhâri), Tome II
creator: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bukhari (Octave Houdas and William Marçais, trans.)
description: The Sahih of al-Bukhari (d. 870) — the most authoritative Sunni hadith collection — in Houdas & Marçais’s complete French translation (Imprimerie nationale, 4 vols., 1903–1914), Tome II.

title: Les Traditions Islamiques (El-Bokhâri), Tome III
creator: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bukhari (Octave Houdas and William Marçais, trans.)
description: The Sahih of al-Bukhari (d. 870) — the most authoritative Sunni hadith collection — in Houdas & Marçais’s complete French translation (Imprimerie nationale, 4 vols., 1903–1914), Tome III.

title: Les Traditions Islamiques (El-Bokhâri), Tome IV
creator: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bukhari (Octave Houdas and William Marçais, trans.)
description: The Sahih of al-Bukhari (d. 870) — the most authoritative Sunni hadith collection — in Houdas & Marçais’s complete French translation (Imprimerie nationale, 4 vols., 1903–1914), Tome IV.

title: The Life of Mohammad, from Original Sources
creator: William Muir (T. H. Weir, rev.)
description: Muir’s Life of Mahomet from original sources (1861; revised by T. H. Weir, 1923) — the great Victorian critical biography built on Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Hisham, Waqidi and Tabari: the PD stand-in for the Sira in English.

title: Alberuni's India, Vol. 1
creator: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (Edward C. Sachau, trans.)
description: Al-Biruni’s India (c. 1030) — the most searching medieval account of Indian religion, philosophy, science and customs ever written by an outsider. Sachau’s English translation (1888), vol. 1.

title: Alberuni's India, Vol. 2
creator: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (Edward C. Sachau, trans.)
description: Al-Biruni’s India (c. 1030) — the most searching medieval account of Indian religion, philosophy, science and customs ever written by an outsider. Sachau’s English translation (1888), vol. 2.

title: The Chronology of Ancient Nations
creator: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni (Edward C. Sachau, trans.)
description: Al-Biruni’s Chronology of Ancient Nations (c. 1000) — comparative calendar science and the festivals of Persians, Jews, Christians and pre-Islamic Arabs. Sachau’s 1879 English version of the Athar-ul-Bakiya.

title: Documents pour servir à l'histoire de l'Inquisition dans le Languedoc
creator: Célestin Douais (ed.)
description: Douais’s 1900 edition of inquisitorial documents from the Languedoc — sentences, depositions and acts from the Doat collection: the raw archive of the medieval Inquisition against the Cathars.

title: The Life of Saladin
creator: Behâ ed-Dîn Ibn Shaddâd
description: Behâ ed-Dîn Ibn Shaddâd’s contemporary Life of Saladin (12th c.) — the intimate portrait of Salah ed-Din by his closest companion and biographer. Palestine Exploration Fund edition (1897).

title: Extrait de la chronique intitulée Kamel-Altevarykh, par Ibn-Alatyr
creator: Ibn al-Athir
description: Ibn al-Athir’s Kamil (al-Kamil fi’l-ta’rikh): the great Mosul chronicle’s account of the Crusades, 1098–1231, in French translation — Recueil des historiens des croisades, Historiens orientaux, Tome 1 (1872).

title: The Great Airship Wave of 1896-1897: Contemporary American Press Accounts
creator: Various newspapers
description: Seventeen verbatim newspaper accounts and editorials from the 1896-1897 American 'mystery airship' wave: the November 1896 California sightings (Sacramento, Oakland, San Francisco, San Jose), the April 1897 Midwest wave (Kansas, Omaha, Chicago), inventor claims, press debate, and early explanations. Transcribed from public-domain scans via the Library of Congress, Chronicling America.

title: The Phantom Airship Waves of 1909-1913: Contemporary Press Accounts
creator: Various newspapers
description: Four verbatim newspaper accounts of the pre-WWI 'phantom airship' scares: the 1909 wave over Britain (Caerphilly Mountain landing report), an American mirage explanation, a Chicago aviator's 'phantom' unmasked, and the 1913 Luneville Zeppelin seizure showing how seriously governments took mystery aircraft. Transcribed from public-domain scans via the Library of Congress, Chronicling America.

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 1
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: John Payne's 1882-84 rendering — the first complete English translation of the Alf Laylah wa Laylah, from the Calcutta (1814-18) Arabic edition. The unexpurgated Victorian rival to Burton's version; vols 1-9 staged complete.

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 2
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 2 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 3
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 3 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 4
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 4 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 5
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 5 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 6
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 6 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 7
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 7 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 8
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 8 of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, Vol. 9 (last)
creator: Anonymous (trans. John Payne)
description: Payne vol. 9 (last) of the first complete English Thousand Nights and One Night (1882-84).

title: Tales from the Arabic, Vol. 1
creator: John Payne
description: Payne's companion set to his Thousand Nights — stories from the Breslau and Calcutta (1814-18) Arabic editions, translated 1884. Vol. 1.

title: Tales from the Arabic, Vol. 2
creator: John Payne
description: Payne's companion set to his Thousand Nights — stories from the Breslau and Calcutta Arabic editions. Vol. 2.

title: Tales from the Arabic, Vol. 3
creator: John Payne
description: Payne's companion set to his Thousand Nights — stories from the Breslau and Calcutta Arabic editions. Vol. 3.

title: The Thousand and One Nights, Vol. 2
creator: Edward William Lane (trans.)
description: Vol. 2 of E. W. Lane's pioneering scholarly Thousand and One Nights (first published 1838-40); completes the library's Lane set.

title: The Thousand and One Nights, Vol. 3
creator: Edward William Lane (trans.)
description: Vol. 3 of E. W. Lane's pioneering scholarly Thousand and One Nights (first published 1838-40); completes the library's Lane set.

title: The Assemblies of Al-Hariri, Vol. 1
creator: Al-Hariri (trans. Thomas Chenery)
description: The first English translation of al-Hariri's Maqamat (Assemblies) — the virtuoso rhymed-prose picaresque of Abu Zayd, a pinnacle of classical Arabic belles-lettres. Chenery's vol. 1 (1867).

title: The Assemblies of Al-Hariri, Vol. 2
creator: Al-Hariri (trans. F. Steingass)
description: Steingass's vol. 2 (1898, Oriental Translation Fund) completing the first English translation of al-Hariri's Maqamat.

title: Antar, a Bedouin Romance (complete, 4 vols.)
creator: Antarah ibn Shaddad (trans. Terrick Hamilton)
description: The first English translation (1819-20) of the Sirah of Antar ibn Shaddad — the romance epic of the pre-Islamic black knight-poet of Arabia, among the longest folk epics in world literature. Complete in one text (4 vols.).

title: The Luzumiyat of Abu'l-Ala
creator: Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri (trans. Ameen Rihani)
description: Ameen Rihani's 1918 selection from the Luzumiyat of Abu'l-Ala al-Ma'arri (973-1057) — the blind Syrian philosopher-poet's skeptical, freethinking verse.

title: The Haft Paikar (The Seven Beauties), Vol. 1: Translation
creator: Nizami Ganjavi (trans. C. E. Wilson)
description: The first complete English translation (1924, Probsthain's Oriental Series) of Nizami's Haft Paikar — the romance of Bahram Gur and the seven princesses, crown of Persian romantic epic. Vol. 1: translation.

title: The Haft Paikar (The Seven Beauties), Vol. 2: Commentary
creator: Nizami Ganjavi (trans. C. E. Wilson)
description: Vol. 2 (commentary) of C. E. Wilson's 1924 Haft Paikar — notes and commentary companion to the first complete English translation.

title: Salaman and Absal
creator: Jami (trans. Edward FitzGerald)
description: Edward FitzGerald's 1856 rendering of Jami's Salaman and Absal — the Sufi allegory of the soul, from the translator of the Rubaiyat.

title: The Shah Nameh of Firdausi
creator: Ferdowsi (trans. James Atkinson)
description: James Atkinson's 1832 rendering — the first English translation of Ferdowsi's Shahnameh (Oriental Translation Fund), abridged in prose and verse.

title: The Chahar Maqala (Four Discourses) of Nizami-i-Arudi
creator: Nizami Arudi (trans. Edward G. Browne)
description: E. G. Browne's revised 1921 translation (Gibb Memorial) of Nizami Arudi's Chahar Maqala — the 12th-century 'Four Discourses' on the secretary, poet, astrologer, and physician.

title: The 'Sacred' Kurral of Tiruvalluva-Nayanar
creator: Tiruvalluvar (trans. G. U. Pope)
description: G. U. Pope's 1886 translation — the first complete English rendering of the Tirukkural, the Tamil classic of 1,330 couplets on virtue (aram), wealth (porul), and love (inbam).

title: The Naladiyar, or Four Hundred Quatrains in Tamil
creator: Anonymous (trans. G. U. Pope)
description: G. U. Pope's 1893 Clarendon Press translation of the Naladiyar — four hundred Tamil quatrains of Jain didactic verse, with critical notes and concordance.

title: The Indian Song of Songs (Gitagovinda)
creator: Jayadeva (trans. Edwin Arnold)
description: Edwin Arnold's 1875 rendering of Jayadeva's Gitagovinda — the 12th-century Sanskrit lyric drama of Radha and Krishna's love, 'the Indian Song of Songs.'

title: The Birth of the War-God (Kumarasambhava)
creator: Kalidasa (trans. Ralph T. H. Griffith)
description: R. T. H. Griffith's 1879 translation (Trubner's Oriental Series) of Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava — the epic of the courtship of Shiva and Parvati and the birth of the war-god.

title: Twenty-two Goblins (Vetala-Panchavimsati)
creator: Sivadasa (trans. Arthur W. Ryder)
description: Arthur W. Ryder's 1917 translation of the Vetala-Panchavimsati (Sivadasa's recension) — the Sanskrit story-cycle of King Vikrama and the riddling goblin.

title: The Harsha-Charita of Bana
creator: Banabhatta (trans. E. B. Cowell & F. W. Thomas)
description: The first English translation (1897, Oriental Translation Fund) of Banabhatta's Harsha-Charita — the 7th-century Sanskrit historical romance of King Harshavardhana.

title: The Kadambari of Bana
creator: Banabhatta (trans. C. M. Ridding)
description: C. M. Ridding's 1896 translation — the first complete English rendering of Banabhatta's Kadambari, the great 7th-century Sanskrit prose romance.

title: The Sarva-Darsana-Samgraha
creator: Madhavacharya (trans. E. B. Cowell & A. E. Gough)
description: E. B. Cowell and A. E. Gough's 1882 translation of Madhava's Sarva-Darsana-Samgraha — the 14th-century review of sixteen systems of Hindu philosophy.

title: A Century of Indian Epigrams (from Bhartrihari)
creator: Bhartrihari (trans. Paul Elmer More)
description: Paul Elmer More's 1898 selection from the satakas of Bhartrihari — the Sanskrit poet of worldly wisdom and renunciation.

title: Chinese Poetry in English Verse
creator: Herbert A. Giles (trans.)
description: Herbert A. Giles's 1898 anthology — the pioneering English-verse rendering of Chinese poetry, from the Book of Odes through the Tang masters Li Bai, Du Fu, and Bai Juyi.

title: Genji Monogatari (The Tale of Genji), Chapters 1-17
creator: Murasaki Shikibu (trans. Kencho Suematsu)
description: Kencho Suematsu's 1882 translation — the first English rendering of Murasaki Shikibu's Tale of Genji (chapters 1-17, abridged), the landmark that introduced the world's first novel to the West.

title: Diaries of Court Ladies of Old Japan
creator: Various (trans. Annie Shepley Omori & Kochi Doi)
description: The first English translation (1920) of three Heian court ladies' diaries — the Sarashina Nikki, the Murasaki Shikibu Nikki, and the Izumi Shikibu Nikki.

title: The Tosa Diary
creator: Ki no Tsurayuki (trans. William N. Porter)
description: William N. Porter's 1912 translation of Ki no Tsurayuki's Tosa Nikki (c. 935) — the 10th-century poetic travel diary, a founding work of Japanese literature.

title: Essays in Idleness (Tsurezuregusa)
creator: Yoshida Kenko (trans. G. B. Sansom)
description: G. B. Sansom's 1911 translation — the first English rendering of Yoshida Kenko's Tsurezuregusa, the 14th-century 'meditations of a recluse.'

title: The Classical Poetry of the Japanese
creator: Basil Hall Chamberlain
description: Basil Hall Chamberlain's 1880 pioneering study — the first systematic English treatment of Japanese classical poetry, with translations from the Manyoshu and Kokinshu.

title: A History of Japanese Literature
creator: W. G. Aston
description: W. G. Aston's 1899 history — the first English history of Japanese literature, by the translator of the Nihongi.

title: The Cloud Dream of the Nine
creator: Kim Man-jung (trans. James S. Gale)
description: James S. Gale's 1922 translation — the first English rendering of Kim Man-jung's Kuunmong (The Cloud Dream of the Nine), the 17th-century Korean Buddhist romance classic.

title: The Literature of the Ancient Egyptians
creator: Adolf Erman (trans. Aylward M. Blackman)
description: Adolf Erman's comprehensive 1927 anthology (translated by Aylward M. Blackman) — poems, narratives, and wisdom texts of ancient Egypt in English.

title: Assyrian and Babylonian Literature: Selected Translations
creator: Robert Francis Harper (ed.)
description: R. F. Harper's 1901 anthology — selected translations of Assyrian and Babylonian literature: creation and flood epics, hymns, royal inscriptions, letters, and laws.

title: The Religious System of the Amazulu
creator: Henry Callaway
description: Bishop Callaway's pioneering record of Zulu religion - Unkulunkulu the first man, ancestor worship, diviners and heaven-doctors - dictated by Zulu converts in their own words, Zulu text facing the English.

title: Specimens of Bushman Folklore
creator: Wilhelm Heinrich Immanuel Bleek and Lucy Catherine Lloyd
description: The |Xam narratives dictated to Bleek and Lloyd in Cape Town - myths, legends and beliefs in the original |Xam with English translation; the founding text of Khoisan ethnography.

title: The Life of a South African Tribe, Vol. 1: The Social Life
creator: Henri Alexandre Junod
description: Vol. 1 (The Social Life) of Junod's Thonga ethnography - kinship, village life and social organization from decades of Swiss missionary fieldwork in Mozambique and the Transvaal.

title: The Life of a South African Tribe, Vol. 2: The Psychic Life
creator: Henri Alexandre Junod
description: Vol. 2 (The Psychic Life): the religion of the Thonga - ancestor worship, magic, divination, possession and the spirit world.

title: Ashanti
creator: Robert Sutherland Rattray
description: Rattray's foundational ethnography of the Ashanti of the Gold Coast - the Golden Stool, abusua kinship, religion and law, from his years as colonial anthropologist.

title: The Ila-Speaking Peoples of Northern Rhodesia, Vol. 1
creator: Edwin William Smith and Andrew Dale
description: Vol. 1 of the classic missionary-administrator ethnography of the Ba-ila of Zambia - economy, kinship and social life.

title: Among the Primitive Bakongo
creator: John H. Weeks
description: Thirty years among the Bakongo of the lower Congo - nkisi fetishism, secret societies, and the religious life of the village, by a Baptist missionary.

title: The Ban of the Bori
creator: Arthur John Newman Tremearne
description: Demons and demon-dancing in West and North Africa - the pioneering English study of the Bori spirit-possession cult of the Hausa.

title: Fetichism in West Africa
creator: Robert Hamill Nassau
description: Forty years' observation of native customs and superstitions on the Gabon coast - fetishism, witchcraft and secret societies by an American Presbyterian missionary.

title: In the Shadow of the Bush
creator: Percy Amaury Talbot
description: Talbot's account of the peoples of southern Nigeria - secret societies, juju and village religion in the Cross River region.

title: Travels in West Africa
creator: Mary Henrietta Kingsley
description: Kingsley's celebrated 1893-95 travels through French Congo, Corisco and the Cameroons - vivid first-hand observation of West African religion, law and daily life.

title: West African Studies
creator: Mary Henrietta Kingsley
description: Kingsley's systematic study of West African religion and law - fetishism, ancestor worship and the sacred logic of native custom; the most influential Victorian account.

title: Among the Ibos of Nigeria
creator: George Thomas Basden
description: Basden's missionary ethnography of the Igbo - chi, ancestors, dibia diviners and the village republic, from thirty-five years in Nigeria.

title: The Voice of Africa
creator: Leo Frobenius
description: Frobenius's 1910-12 expedition account - Yoruba, Nupe and Jukun religion and art in the Western Sudan; the book that carried African sacred art to Europe.

title: The Native Tribes of Central Australia
creator: Baldwin Spencer and Francis James Gillen
description: The founding classic of Australian anthropology - Arunta totemism, the Alcheringa, initiation rites and magic, from the Horn expedition and years at Alice Springs.

title: The Native Tribes of South-East Australia
creator: Alfred William Howitt
description: Howitt's magnum opus on the Kurnai, Wiradjuri and neighbouring peoples - kinship systems, initiation, and magic among the south-eastern tribes.

title: The Melanesians of British New Guinea
creator: Charles Gabriel Seligman
description: The Cambridge expedition's New Guinea volume - sorcery, secret societies and mortuary ritual on the Papuan coast, with a chapter by F. R. Barton.

title: The Melanesians: Studies in their Anthropology and Folk-Lore
creator: Robert Henry Codrington
description: The book that gave anthropology the word 'mana' - Codrington's Melanesian mission ethnography: secret societies, ghosts, and the spiritual power behind magic.

title: Myths and Songs from the South Pacific
creator: William Wyatt Gill
description: Mangaian and Cook Islands myths and songs collected by missionary W. W. Gill - creation, the underworld Avaiki, and the gods of Polynesia in native verse.

title: Polynesian Religion
creator: Edward Smith Craighill Handy
description: Handy's Bishop Museum synthesis of Polynesian religion - tapu, mana, gods and ritual across Hawaii, Tahiti, Samoa and New Zealand.

title: An Account of the Natives of the Tonga Islands
creator: William Mariner (John Martin, ed.)
description: Mariner's four years among the Tongans (1806-10) as edited by John Martin - gods, taboo, burial rites and war customs; the earliest intimate account of Polynesian life.

title: Coming of Age in Samoa
creator: Margaret Mead
description: Mead's famous study of Samoan adolescence - custom, rank, and the religious regulation of youth in Polynesia; the book that made anthropology famous.

title: Malay Magic
creator: Walter William Skeat
description: Skeat's classic on Malay folk religion - spirits, charms, divination and the pawang's craft, gathered in Selangor and the Malay states.

title: Pagan Races of the Malay Peninsula, Vol. 1
creator: Walter William Skeat and Charles Otto Blagden
description: Vol. 1 of the great survey of the Semang, Sakai and Jakun - physical anthropology and material life of the peninsula's aborigines.

title: Pagan Races of the Malay Peninsula, Vol. 2
creator: Walter William Skeat and Charles Otto Blagden
description: Vol. 2: the religion, folklore and language of the peninsula's pagan races - shamanism, soul-beliefs and magic.

title: The Pagan Tribes of Borneo, Vol. 1
creator: Charles Hose and William McDougall
description: Vol. 1 of Hose and McDougall's Borneo ethnography - the Kayans, Kenyahs and Klemantans: longhouse life, omen-birds and social order.

title: The Pagan Tribes of Borneo, Vol. 2
creator: Charles Hose and William McDougall
description: Vol. 2: religion and magic in Borneo - soul beliefs, shamanism, headhunting ritual and the cult of the omen-birds.

title: The Angami Nagas
creator: John Henry Hutton
description: Hutton's administrator-ethnography of the Angami Nagas of the Assam hills - feasts of merit, ancestor cult and village government.

title: The Sema Nagas
creator: John Henry Hutton
description: The companion volume on the Sema (Sumi) Nagas - morungs, headhunting, and the religion of the Assam hill tribes.

title: The Khasis
creator: Philip Richard Thornhagh Gurdon
description: Gurdon's ethnography of the matrilineal Khasis of Assam - ancestor worship, divination, and the sacred forests.

title: Peoples of Asiatic Russia
creator: Waldemar Jochelson
description: Jochelson's survey of the peoples of Asiatic Russia - Yukaghir, Koryak and Tungus social life and shamanism, from the Jesup North Pacific Expedition.

title: Notes on the Iroquois
creator: Henry Rowe Schoolcraft
description: Schoolcraft's classic on the Iroquois confederacy - mythology, government, and the condolence council, with Iroquois pictographs.

title: Letters and Notes on the Manners, Customs, and Conditions of the North American Indians, Vol. 1
creator: George Catlin
description: Vol. 1 of Catlin's 1832-39 travels among the Plains and western tribes - Mandan O-kee-pa, buffalo-hunt ritual and village life, from his letters and paintings.

title: Letters and Notes on the Manners, Customs, and Conditions of the North American Indians, Vol. 2
creator: George Catlin
description: Vol. 2: the western prairies, Comanche and the Rocky Mountain tribes - sun dance, medicine rites and the vanishing buffalo world.

title: The Sacred Formulas of the Cherokees
creator: James Mooney
description: Mooney's Cherokee sacred formulas - medicine, hunting and love charms dictated by Cherokee shamans, in Cherokee with English translation (7th BAE Annual Report).

title: Calendar History of the Kiowa Indians
creator: James Mooney
description: Set-t'an's winter-count pictographs with Mooney's history of the Kiowa - sun dance, tribal wars and the reservation years (17th BAE Annual Report).

title: Blackfoot Lodge Tales
creator: George Bird Grinnell
description: Grinnell's Blackfoot myths and histories - Napi the trickster, the beaver medicine, and star legends from the northern Plains.

title: Pawnee Hero Stories and Folk-Tales
creator: George Bird Grinnell
description: Pawnee hero tales and folk narratives - Tirawa, the morning-star sacrifice, and the warrior societies of the Plains.

title: The Cheyenne Indians, Vol. 1
creator: George Bird Grinnell
description: Vol. 1 (History and Society): Grinnell's definitive Cheyenne ethnography - the arrow renewal, tribal government and the old nomadic life.

title: Tsimshian Mythology
creator: Franz Boas
description: Boas's Tsimshian mythology from texts dictated by Henry Tate - Raven legends and crest myths of the northern Northwest Coast (31st BAE Annual Report).

title: The Religion of the Kwakiutl Indians
creator: Franz Boas
description: Boas on Kwakwaka'wakw religion - winter ceremonial, secret societies and shamanism, from dictated native texts (Columbia University Contributions to Anthropology).

title: Primitive Man as Philosopher
creator: Paul Radin
description: Radin's landmark argument that 'primitive' peoples philosophize - Winnebago thinkers on religion, fate, and the nature of things.

title: Crashing Thunder: The Autobiography of an American Indian
creator: Paul Radin
description: The autobiography of a Winnebago Indian, dictated to Radin - a first-person life of visions, peyote, and the Thunderbird clan.

title: Tlingit Myths and Texts
creator: John Reed Swanton
description: Tlingit myths and texts recorded by Swanton - Raven cycle, crest stories and shaman narratives (BAE Bulletin 39).

title: Haida Texts and Myths
creator: John Reed Swanton
description: Haida texts and myths in the Skidegate dialect - Raven, potlatch and the spirit world of Haida Gwaii (BAE Bulletin 29).

title: Navaho Legends
creator: Washington Matthews
description: Matthews's Navajo legends - the Night Chant, Mountain Chant and creation myths collected by the army surgeon-ethnographer.

title: Zuni Folk Tales
creator: Frank Hamilton Cushing
description: Cushing's Zuni folk tales - Coyote, the twin war gods, and the emergence myth, from his years living at Zuni Pueblo.

title: Omaha Sociology
creator: James Owen Dorsey
description: Dorsey's Omaha sociology - gentes, the sacred tents, and the tribal circle (3rd BAE Annual Report).

title: A Study of Siouan Cults
creator: James Owen Dorsey
description: Dorsey's comparative study of Siouan religion - Omaha, Ponka, Osage and Dakota cults, societies and mysteries (11th BAE Annual Report).

title: Indian Story and Song from North America
creator: Alice Cunningham Fletcher
description: Fletcher's collection of Omaha, Pawnee and other tribal songs with stories - music as the record of ritual life.

title: The American Indian
creator: Clark Wissler
description: Wissler's introduction to the anthropology of the New World - culture areas, the vision quest, and the diffusion of ritual.

title: Among the Indians of Guiana
creator: Everard Ferdinand im Thurn
description: im Thurn's Guiana classic - Carib and Arawak religion, the peaiman, and spirit beliefs of the forest tribes.

title: Legends and Myths of the Aboriginal Indians of British Guiana
creator: William Henry Brett
description: Missionary Brett's collection of Guiana Indian legends - Makonaima, the great flood, and Arawak-Carib mythology.

title: An Inquiry into the Animism and Folk-lore of the Guiana Indians
creator: Walter Edmund Roth
description: Roth's systematic inquiry into Guiana Indian animism - soul beliefs, kanaima, and the spirit world (BAE Bulletin 30).

title: Researches into the Early History of Mankind and the Development of Civilization
creator: Edward Burnett Tylor
description: Tylor's first great work - the method of survivals, gesture-language, and the argument for psychic unity that led to Primitive Culture.

title: Custom and Myth
creator: Andrew Lang
description: Lang's essays defending the 'savage' origin of myths - totemism, the bull-roarer, and the irrational element in classical myth.

title: Modern Mythology
creator: Andrew Lang
description: Lang's reply to Max Muller - myth as the survival of savage thought, not a 'disease of language'.

title: Totemism and Exogamy, Vol. 1
creator: James George Frazer
description: Vol. 1 of Frazer's four-volume treatise on totemism and exogamy - the great comparative survey of clan organization and marriage regulation.

title: Totemism and Exogamy, Vol. 2
creator: James George Frazer
description: Vol. 2 of Frazer's four-volume treatise - totemism in Australia, Africa and the Americas.

title: Totemism and Exogamy, Vol. 3
creator: James George Frazer
description: Vol. 3 of Frazer's four-volume treatise - exogamy, totemic taboos and the origin of the clan system.

title: Totemism and Exogamy, Vol. 4
creator: James George Frazer
description: Vol. 4 of Frazer's four-volume treatise - the theory of totemism and its relation to religion.

title: Psyche's Task
creator: James George Frazer
description: Frazer's discourse on the influence of superstition on the growth of institutions - how taboo and magic built government, property and marriage.

title: Primitive Religion
creator: Robert Harry Lowie
description: Lowie's systematic survey of religious belief among stateless peoples - the founding textbook of the anthropology of religion.

title: Culture and Ethnology
creator: Robert Harry Lowie
description: Lowie's early essays on diffusion, convergence, and the culture concept - the Boasian program in miniature.

title: The Todas
creator: W. H. R. Rivers
description: Rivers's Toda ethnography - the buffalo dairy ritual, polyandry, and the kinship algebra that launched British social anthropology.

title: The History of Melanesian Society, Vol. 1
creator: W. H. R. Rivers
description: Vol. 1 of Rivers's diffusionist history - secret societies, kava ritual and the peopling of Melanesia.

title: The History of Melanesian Society, Vol. 2
creator: W. H. R. Rivers
description: Vol. 2: kinship terminologies and the reconstruction of Melanesian social history.

title: Magic and Fetishism
creator: Alfred Cort Haddon
description: Haddon's Torres Straits synthesis - the theory of magic and fetishism from the Cambridge expedition's fieldwork.

title: The Study of Man
creator: Alfred Cort Haddon
description: Haddon's introduction to anthropology - race, custom and the ethnology of the Torres Straits.

title: The Mystic Rose: A Study of Primitive Marriage

title: How Natives Think

description: Levy-Bruhl's famous thesis of 'primitive mentality' - collective representations and participation mystique (Clare's 1926 authorized English translation).

title: The Religions of Primitive Peoples
creator: Daniel Garrison Brinton

title: Early Civilization: An Introduction to Anthropology
creator: Alexander Goldenweiser

title: Chamber Music

title: Exiles

title: Pomes Penyeach
creator: James Joyce

title: The Sacred Wood
creator: T. S. Eliot

title: Homage to John Dryden
creator: T. S. Eliot

title: For Lancelot Andrewes
creator: T. S. Eliot

creator: T. S. Eliot

title: Ara Vos Prec
creator: T. S. Eliot

title: Ideas of Good and Evil

title: Responsibilities

title: Per Amica Silentia Lunae
creator: W. B. Yeats

title: The Trespasser

title: The Prussian Officer and Other Stories

title: Amores
creator: D. H. Lawrence

title: Psychoanalysis and the Unconscious

title: The Boy in the Bush
creator: D. H. Lawrence

title: The Rescue

creator: Alfred North Whitehead

title: The Realm of Matter: Book Second of Realms of Being

title: Commentaries on the Constitution of the United States, Vol. I

title: Commentaries on American Law, Vol. I

title: The History of English Law before the Time of Edward I, Vol. I

title: The Geneva Bible (1560)
creator: William Whittingham and others
description: The Geneva Bible of 1560 — the first full edition of the Bible of the English exiles at Geneva (Whittingham, Coverdale, Goodman, Gilby, Sampson, Cole); the first English Bible with verse divisions, the Bible of Shakespeare and the Pilgrims. Complete Old and New Testaments with Apocrypha, from a 1560 printing.

title: The Great Bible (1539)
creator: Myles Coverdale
description: The Great Bible of 1539 — 'the Byble in Englyshe', the first authorized English Bible, prepared by Myles Coverdale under Thomas Cromwell and set up in every English parish; the revision of Matthew's Bible that the Geneva translators then revised in turn. Complete Old and New Testaments.

title: Matthew's Bible (1537)
creator: John Rogers (as Thomas Matthew)
description: Matthew's Bible of 1537 — John Rogers' compilation under the pseudonym Thomas Matthew, combining Tyndale's New Testament and Pentateuch with Coverdale's rendering of the rest; the pivotal bridge edition between Tyndale and the Great Bible, the first Bible printed in England under royal licence. Complete Old and New Testaments.

title: Biblia: Die gantze Heilige Schrifft Deudsch (Luther, 1545)
creator: Martin Luther
description: The Luther Bible of 1545 — 'Biblia: das ist: Die gantze Heilige Schrifft Deudsch, auffs new zugerichtet', printed by Hans Lufft at Wittenberg; the last edition overseen by Luther himself ('Ausgabe letzter Hand'), the translation that shaped the German language. Complete Bible in the original Early New High German.

title: Forerunners and Rivals of Christianity, Vol. 1: From 330 B.C. to 330 A.D.
creator: Francis Legge
description: Francis Legge's history of Christianity's forerunners and rivals — Vol. 1 (1915), covering the pre-Christian religious world: Alexander's conquests, the Alexandrian divinities, the origin of Gnosticism, and the pre-Christian Gnostics. Companion to the already-hosted Vol. 2 on the post-Christian Gnostic systems.

title: The Apostolic Tradition of Hippolytus (Easton translation)
creator: Hippolytus of Rome; translated by Burton Scott Easton
description: Burton Scott Easton's 1934 English translation — with introduction and notes — of Hippolytus of Rome's Apostolic Tradition (c. 215 AD), the earliest surviving church order, describing early Christian ordination, baptism, and eucharistic practice in detail. Public domain (Project Gutenberg).

title: Compendium Maleficarum
creator: Francesco Maria Guazzo (Montague Summers, trans./ed.)
description: Guazzo's 1608 witch-hunter's manual in Montague Summers's 1929 English translation: the classic early-modern demonology of witchcraft prosecution and its remedies.

title: Philosophie als strenge Wissenschaft
creator: Edmund Husserl
description: Husserl's 1911 programmatic essay 'Philosophy as Rigorous Science' (Logos, vol. I): the founding manifesto of the phenomenological movement. Extracted from the complete Logos I volume; German.

title: The Jesuit Relations and Allied Documents, Vol. 26
creator: Reuben Gold Thwaites (ed.)
description: Vol. 26 (Lower Canada) of Reuben Gold Thwaites's 73-volume edition of the Jesuit Relations (1896-1901): the foundational documentary corpus of the North American indigenous missions. Completes vols. 1-30.

title: The Institutes of Justinian
creator: Justinian I (J. B. Moyle, trans.)
description: Moyle's translation of Justinian's Institutes (1906 ed.): alternate English rendering to the Sandars 1874 translation already in the library.

title: Second Characters; or, The Language of Forms
creator: Anthony Ashley Cooper, Earl of Shaftesbury (Benjamin Rand, ed.)
description: Shaftesbury's Second Characters (ed. Benjamin Rand, 1914): the posthumous second series of the Characteristics, on art, aesthetics and the language of forms.

title: The Damnable Life and Death of One Stubbe Peeter, a Most Wicked Sorcerer
creator: Anonymous
description: The 1590 English pamphlet on Peter Stumpp (Stubbe Peeter), executed 1589 for murders, lycanthropy and witchcraft: the founding werewolf pamphlet of early modern England.

title: Textes philosophiques
creator: Léon Wieger
description: Wieger's 1906 French collection of Chinese philosophical and religious texts. French.

title: A Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy, Vol. 1
creator: Thomas Young
description: Vol. 1 of Thomas Young's 1807 Course of Lectures on Natural Philosophy and the Mechanical Arts: the polymath's great physics lectures. Completes the set with Vol. 2 (already in the library).
